title: Circle defends USDC economics as stablecoin rivals court its partners with bigger cut
summary: Coinbase, Circle’s largest USDC partner, also backs Open USD, a rival network that passes reserve income to partners after a management fee.
content:
Oct 17, 2026, 9:06 p.m. EDT

2 min read

Summary

  • Circle said it kept about 7 cents of profit per revenue dollar in the first half of 2026, after $819 million of $1.4 billion went to distribution and transaction costs.
  • Coinbase, Circle’s largest USDC partner, also backs Open USD, a rival network that passes reserve income to partners after a management fee.
  • Circle argued reserve income must also fund redemption, compliance and liquidity, and says standard USDC redemptions remain free.

Stablecoin issuer Circle CRCL$82.25·Market Closed is defending its business model as Coinbase, its largest distribution partner, backs a rival that aims to give businesses more income from stablecoin reserves.

In a blog post on Friday, Chief Commercial Officer Kash Razzaghi wrote that Circle kept about 7 cents in net profit for each dollar in revenue made during the first half of 2026. The firm brought in about $1.4 billion, while distribution and transaction costs totaled $819 million.

The post puts the figures at the center of a dispute over who gets the interest earned on assets backing stablecoins.

Circle said the remaining $473 million covered compliance, liquidity and product development. That figure also included about $214 million in stock-based compensation and related costs.

Coinbase is Circle’s largest USDC partner, but is also a backer of Open USD, along with Stripe and BlackRock. Open USD, unveiled in June, aims to let businesses mint and redeem stablecoins without fees, while passing off reserve income minus a management fee to participants.

Circle's post did not name Open USD, whose OUSD token is now live, directly, and there are other competitors like the Paxos-led Global Dollar Network (USDG) that also share reserve income with participants.

"The costs of redemption, compliance, and resilience don't disappear just because the issuer declined to pay them," Razzaghi wrote.

Circle has also been working to secure additional distribution partners. In September, Binance bought a $100 million stake in the firm under a five-year deal that includes a fee tied to USDC held through Circle's wallet service.

Circle said standard USDC redemptions remain free and "typically settle in up to two business days." Qualifying platform customers and payment flows through Circle Payments Network can now access near-real-time redemptions at no cost, it said.

title: Pump.fun Brings Hyperliquid Perps to Its Meme Coin Empire
summary: Pump.fun has expanded beyond its Solana meme coin business, introducing perpetual futures trading powered by Hyperliquid. The new interface offers leveraged cryptocurrency trading while charging builder fees of up to 0.10% per order and bridge fees reaching 0.25%. However, traders in the United Stat...
content:
1. News
  2. Featured
  3. Pump.fun Brings Hyperliquid Perps to Its Meme Coin Empire

Published:Oct 17, 2026, 8:30 PM EDT

Pump.fun has expanded beyond its Solana meme coin business, introducing perpetual futures trading powered by Hyperliquid. The new interface offers leveraged cryptocurrency trading while charging builder fees of up to 0.10% per order and bridge fees reaching 0.25%. However, traders in the United States and Ontario are barred from using the feature, according to terms updated Oct. 17, 2026.

WRITTEN BY

SHARE

Published: Oct 17, 2026, 8:30 PM EDT

Key Takeaways

  • Pump.fun introduced Hyperliquid-powered perpetual futures trading on Oct. 17, 2026.
  • Pump.fun charges up to 0.10% per futures order and 0.25% per bridge transfer.
  • Pump.fun excludes U.S. and Ontario users while Hyperliquid manages trading and liquidations.

Pump.fun Brings Hyperliquid Perpetual Futures to Its Trading Platform

Pump.fun built its reputation helping traders create and speculate on Solana meme coins. Now the memecoin launchpad is moving into a different corner of cryptocurrency trading, offering leveraged perpetual futures through the perps decentralized exchange (DEX) Hyperliquid.

The expansion, detailed in updated terms published Oct. 17, 2026, introduces another potential revenue stream for Pump.fun without requiring the company to operate its own derivatives exchange.

Hyperliquid Handles the Trading While Pump.fun Collects Fees

The new interface allows users to trade perpetual futures, contracts that let traders speculate on cryptocurrency prices without owning the underlying assets or facing a fixed expiration date.

Pump.fun provides the interface, while Hyperliquid handles order matching, collateral, funding payments and liquidations. Users retain control of their wallets, and their positions remain accessible through Hyperliquid even if Pump.fun access disappears. Earlier trading data indicated support for bitcoin contracts offering up to 40x leverage and ethereum contracts reaching 25x.

Under Pump.fun’s updated fee schedule, the platform can charge up to 0.10% of an order’s value when traders open, increase or close positions. That translates into a $10 builder fee on a $10,000 trade. Moving funds through the integrated bridge carries another fee of up to 0.25%, meaning a $1,000 transfer could cost $2.50 before outside charges. Hyperliquid’s own trading fees and other third-party costs apply separately.

American and Ontario Traders Face Restrictions

Pump.fun’s updated terms prohibit U.S. users, including those in American territories, and Ontario users from accessing perpetual futures. Restrictions also cover sanctioned jurisdictions and other prohibited individuals. The platform prohibits using VPNs to evade these limitations. Leveraged trading introduces another complication. A relatively small adverse price movement can wipe out collateral, with Hyperliquid automatically liquidating positions when margin requirements are breached.

For Pump.fun, the expansion opens another fee-generating business beyond meme coins. For traders, the opportunity comes with borrowing-like exposure, multiple charges and the possibility of losing an entire position.

title: Goldman Sachs CEO Sees Tokenization as Wall Street’s Next Act
summary: Goldman Sachs CEO David Solomon sees tokenization reshaping financial markets, potentially opening new revenue opportunities rather than simply threatening traditional finance (TradFi) and Wall Street businesses. During the bank’s Oct. 13 earnings call, Solomon detailed tokenized bonds, money market...
content:
Goldman Sachs CEO David Solomon sees tokenization reshaping financial markets, potentially opening new revenue opportunities rather than simply threatening traditional finance (TradFi) and Wall Street businesses. During the bank’s Oct. 13 earnings call, Solomon detailed tokenized bonds, money market funds, real estate, and participation in DTCC’s tokenization service. The discussion also touched on decentralized finance (DeFi), prediction markets, and automated trading, although Solomon cautioned that blockchain-based activity remains relatively small.

Key Takeaways

  • Goldman Sachs CEO David Solomon sees tokenization expanding opportunities across financial markets.
  • Goldman Sachs joined DTCC’s tokenization service launch in July and is exploring scalable applications.
  • Goldman Sachs discussed DeFi and prediction markets but announced no specific products in either sector.

Goldman Sachs CEO David Solomon Sees Opportunity in Blockchain’s Challenge to Wall Street

Wall Street’s established trading machinery is facing a new technological challenge, and Goldman Sachs CEO David Solomon isn’t sounding the alarm. During the investment bank’s third-quarter earnings call on Oct. 13, Solomon described tokenization as an important development across financial markets, outlining investments in blockchain infrastructure and tokenized assets.

The conversation began with a pointed question about whether things like DeFi, prediction markets and automated trading might chip away at Goldman’s lucrative markets business. Solomon’s response suggested the opposite possibility. These emerging technologies might ultimately bring the banking giant more products, more clients and considerably more business.

From DeFi Vaults to Prediction Markets, Goldman Faces a New Trading Era

Evercore ISI analyst Glenn Schorr raised the stakes by naming tokenization, agentic trading, defi vaults and prediction markets as potential challengers to Goldman’s trading operations. Solomon acknowledged the technological shift but pointed to electronic equities trading as an earlier example of disruption that Goldman successfully navigated.

“Today, tokenization is obviously an important trend. We see it across asset classes,” Solomon remarked during the call. The CEO argued that emerging market structures can introduce new products, attract clients and broaden distribution, effectively expanding the bank’s total addressable market.

His remarks did not announce a Goldman prediction market, DeFi vault or agentic trading product. Instead, they positioned these developments within a broader transformation of financial infrastructure that the bank intends to monitor and participate in.

Tokenized Bonds, Real Estate and Money Market Funds Already in Play

Goldman isn’t merely watching from the sidelines. Solomon pointed to years of investments in digital asset companies and market infrastructure, alongside its proprietary GS DAP platform, which provides blockchain-based infrastructure for financial assets. “We’ve tokenized bonds. We have a number of money market funds that are tokenized, real estate for certain clients,” Solomon explained.

The bank also participated in the July launch of the Depository Trust & Clearing Corp.’s (DTCC) tokenization service and is evaluating applications that can operate at greater scale. The attraction is straightforward. Tokenization can represent ownership of traditional assets digitally, potentially making transfers, recordkeeping and settlement more efficient.

Solomon expects the technology to reduce costs, automate processes and improve liquidity across asset classes. Still, he threw cold water on expectations of an immediate financial revolution, characterizing existing activity as small.

Goldman Sachs Backs Regulatory Clarity While Agencies Advance Rules

Regulation also figured prominently in Solomon’s assessment. He confirmed that Goldman publicly supported passage of the CLARITY legislation, despite reservations about its provisions. “We were publicly supportive of CLARITY passing. It wasn’t perfect, but we thought it would be good to give the market more clarity, no pun intended, and ensure investor protection,” he remarked.

Solomon added that regulatory agencies are already pursuing clearer market rules, with Goldman actively participating in those discussions. For a bank operating across traditional securities and emerging digital asset markets, regulatory certainty is central to determining which products can reach institutional clients.

A $6.4 Billion Equities Business Meets Blockchain Innovation

The discussion arrived against an impressive financial backdrop. Goldman reported $18.68 billion in quarterly net revenue, while equities revenue climbed 72% year over year to $6.4 billion. Equities financing revenue reached a record $3.37 billion, nearly doubling from a year earlier. Chief Financial Officer Denis Coleman also reported $12.7 billion in combined financing revenue across equities and fixed income, currencies and commodities for the first nine months.

Those figures illustrate the established business that blockchain-based competitors hope to challenge, and the financial resources Goldman can deploy in response. Solomon’s argument was that technological change doesn’t necessarily eliminate established intermediaries. It can create additional opportunities for institutions capable of adapting.

For now, the distinction is striking. Prediction markets and defi vaults entered the conversation as possible competitive threats, while tokenization emerged as an area of concrete investment and experimentation. Goldman has the infrastructure, the capital and the interest. What it hasn’t demonstrated is how much revenue these emerging markets will ultimately deliver in a world still dominated by TradFi systems.

title: Strive Bitcoin Holdings Reach 35,595 BTC As Wall Street Raises Price Target 27%
summary: TL;DR: TD Cowen reportedly raised its Strive share-price target from $44 to $56 after the Bitcoin treasury company expanded its holdings to 35,595 BTC. Strive is also seeking financing through a substantial preferred-share offering. Bitcoin treasury company Strive is attracting fresh attention from ...
content:
TL;DR: TD Cowen reportedly raised its Strive share-price target from $44 to $56 after the Bitcoin treasury company expanded its holdings to 35,595 BTC. Strive is also seeking financing through a substantial preferred-share offering.

Bitcoin treasury company Strive is attracting fresh attention from Wall Street after a rapid buying programme took its reported holdings to 35,595 BTC.

TD Cowen analysts increased their share-price target on Strive from $44 to $56 in an October 16 research update, pointing to the pace of the company’s Bitcoin acquisitions.

The company has accumulated thousands of BTC in a matter of weeks, considerably exceeding some earlier analyst expectations.

A Growing Treasury Needs Funding

Strive’s strategy depends on raising capital and acquiring additional Bitcoin. Its announced purchases have positioned it among the larger corporate holders, though still far behind Strategy.

The firm also announced pricing for a substantial preferred stock offering. Seven million shares at $90 each would generate approximately $630 million in gross proceeds before expenses, assuming completion on the announced terms.

Such financing can raise cash without the immediate dilution associated with issuing common shares, but preferred dividends create their own ongoing costs.

Strive has repeatedly expanded its Bitcoin holdings, including a previously reported purchase that lifted its treasury above 26,000 BTC.

Bitcoin Per Share Is The Real Test

A rising total BTC balance does not automatically mean existing shareholders benefit if the company simultaneously expands its share count or adds expensive financing obligations.

For that reason, investors must assess Bitcoin holdings alongside the capital structure supporting them.

TD Cowen’s higher target signals optimism about Strive’s execution, but remains an analyst opinion rather than a guaranteed future price.

The company’s next financing and treasury disclosures will show whether it can keep increasing Bitcoin exposure on terms that make economic sense for shareholders.

Written by the News Desk and edited by Samuel Rae.

title: Pantera Leads $10 Million Fission Funding Round To Solve Tokenized Fund Liquidity Problem
summary: TL;DR: Tokenization infrastructure firm Fission has raised $10 million in a funding round led by Pantera Capital. It wants to make it easier for eligible investors to sell tokenized private-market holdings without waiting for traditional fund redemption periods. The tokenization industry has spent y...
content:
TL;DR: Tokenization infrastructure firm Fission has raised $10 million in a funding round led by Pantera Capital. It wants to make it easier for eligible investors to sell tokenized private-market holdings without waiting for traditional fund redemption periods.

The tokenization industry has spent years promising faster transfers of financial assets. Fission now wants to solve a more difficult problem: what happens when an investor wants their money back?

The financial technology company announced on October 15 that it had raised $10 million in a round led by Pantera Capital, with participation from Circle Ventures and other investors.

Its business focuses on liquidity for tokenized alternative investments, including private funds that are traditionally difficult to sell quickly.

A Token Is Not The Same As A Buyer

Representing ownership of a fund on a blockchain may make recordkeeping and transfers more efficient. It does not automatically create a liquid market.

A private credit or private equity fund can still have transfer restrictions, limited redemption windows and few willing buyers.

Fission is developing infrastructure to provide secondary-market liquidity for qualifying interests. Some transactions can be completed rapidly when liquidity is available, but that should not be confused with a guaranteed right to sell every asset instantly at full value.

The company’s approach complements the industry’s wider interest in tokenized institutional investment products.

The Next Stage Of Tokenization

Investors increasingly want to know how tokenized assets can be financed, transferred and redeemed, not simply how they are issued.

Fission plans to use the money to extend its infrastructure and support more asset managers.

Pantera’s investment suggests that solving practical market problems may be at least as commercially significant as launching another blockchain-based security.

Written by the News Desk and edited by Samuel Rae.

title: Why Stablecoins May Never Escape Traditional Banking Risks: Frgmnt CEO
summary: As stablecoins transition from decentralized finance tools to essential infrastructure for accessing U.S. dollars, an expert says their next phase of adoption depends on making blockchain technology invisible to the end user. From Speculative Tools to Digital Dollar Access When the first wave of dec...
content:
As stablecoins transition from decentralized finance tools to essential infrastructure for accessing U.S. dollars, an expert says their next phase of adoption depends on making blockchain technology invisible to the end user.

Key Takeaways

  • Following 2023 bank failures, Frgmnt CEO Aurélien Roussel urged stablecoin issuers to diversify reserves.
  • Tether leads global trade, but MiCA regulations force issuers to build 100% compliant local infrastructure.
  • Sub-cent Layer 2 transaction costs will drive stablecoins beyond payments into yield-generating capital.

From Speculative Tools to Digital Dollar Access

When the first wave of decentralized finance (DeFi) swept through the global economy, stablecoins were primarily viewed as speculative lubricants, but that narrative is rapidly fading away. In emerging markets and across global commercial corridors, stablecoins are about access to the U.S. dollar.

As global macroeconomic environments shift, the mainstream adoption of digital fiat is pivoting from speculative yield-chasing toward everyday economic utility. Yet, as billions of dollars shift into digital formats, a fundamental financial question emerges: What happens to those dollars when they are not being used?

Aurélien Roussel, co-founder and CEO of Frgmnt, a stablecoin infrastructure company, believes the industry stands at a critical juncture. Having previously served as chief operating officer at Bricks.co, Roussel understands both the frictions of legacy finance and the power of technological scale.

Indeed, for users in emerging economies, the stablecoin value proposition has never been about complex DeFi protocols. According to Roussel, it is about basic economic survival that is protecting purchasing power against local currency depreciation, and moving capital without the crushing friction of traditional banking rails.

“I think the biggest shift is that stablecoins are becoming less about crypto and more about access to dollars,” explained Roussel. “That user doesn’t necessarily care about DeFi yields. They care about reliability, liquidity, and cost.”

According to Roussel, the next phase of global adoption will occur through products where the underlying blockchain becomes nearly invisible—embedded directly into remittances, payroll, corporate treasury, and merchant settlement.

“Once a user or business already holds digital dollars, a natural question follows: What happens to those dollars when they are not being used? This is where I think the distinction between transactional liquidity and productive liquidity becomes important,” he said. “The same dollar can remain liquid and available for payments while being deployed into a carefully managed strategy when it is idle.”

Rather than forcing mainstream users to become DeFi experts, Roussel argues that the industry’s job is to make the underlying infrastructure robust enough that users benefit automatically, without ever having to think about the underlying technical components.

Managing Banking Sector Counterparty Risks

The banking failures of 2023 exposed a core paradox of fiat-collateralized stablecoins: While they exist as decentralized, programmable assets onchain, they remain anchored to highly centralized, legacy banking institutions offchain.

This raises an important question: Can fiat-backed stablecoins ever truly decouple from traditional banking risk? Roussel is pragmatic.

“I don’t think a fiat-backed stablecoin can ever be completely decoupled from the traditional financial system. The question is how that dependency is structured and how much resilience is built around it,” he said. “The lesson from previous banking failures is that stablecoin infrastructure needs to assume that individual banking counterparties can fail.”

To safeguard against systemic failures, Roussel points to modular architecture as the essential roadmap for stablecoin issuers.

One way of achieving this is through diversification of banking relationships to eliminate single-point-of-failure counterparty risk. Segregation of reserves, transparent and real-time attestations, and operational redundancy across multiple liquidity venues and redemption mechanisms are other safeguards against systemic failures.

“Blockchain doesn’t eliminate traditional financial risk,” Roussel noted. “What it can do is make parts of the financial architecture more transparent, programmable, and auditable. The objective should therefore not be to pretend that stablecoins are completely independent from traditional finance, but to make those dependencies visible, diversified, and manageable.”

Tether’s USDT has long maintained a dominant grip on global non-Western trade due to deeply entrenched network effects. While regulatory compliance and institutional structuring are often touted as competitive moats, Roussel emphasized that compliance alone will not automatically unseat entrenched liquidity.

“Network effects are extremely powerful in money,” said Roussel. “Once a stablecoin has deep liquidity, broad exchange support, merchant acceptance, and strong distribution in a particular market, replacing it becomes difficult.”

However, Roussel does not view the market as a winner-take-all arena. Instead, he foresees a segmented ecosystem where different stablecoins specialize in distinct use cases ranging from retail payments and corporate treasury management to institutional settlement and long-term savings.

“For institutional users in particular, the decision is likely to depend increasingly on transparency, liquidity, regulatory access, custody, redemption, and integration with existing financial infrastructure,” Roussel said. “So I expect the stablecoin market to become more segmented rather than simply converging on one global winner. The important competitive advantage will increasingly be distribution and infrastructure, not simply the token itself.”

Navigating Regulatory Balkanization

As jurisdictions establish localized legal frameworks, such as Europe’s Markets in Crypto-Assets (MiCA) regulation and various regional initiatives, issuers face a fragmented landscape. This regulatory fragmentation forces infrastructure to adapt across geographic lines.

Yet, Roussel believes that regulatory friction will not halt global adoption, drawing a direct parallel to the evolution of the broader internet.

“The internet itself operates across very different legal systems,” Roussel said. “What emerged was not one global regulatory framework, but common technical infrastructure combined with local rules at the points where that infrastructure interacts with regulated economies. I expect something similar with stablecoins.”

The primary threat, according to Roussel, is the potential creation of isolated, jurisdiction-specific technical silos that destroy cross-border interoperability.

“The industry should aim for regulatory interoperability, even if full regulatory harmonization is unrealistic,” he advocated. “Standards around reserve transparency, attestations, identity, compliance, and redemption could become increasingly interoperable across jurisdictions. In that model, the protocol layer remains global, while regulated access points are localized.”

Meanwhile, as central banks globally pilot central bank digital currencies (CBDCs), questions arise over whether sovereign tokens will crowd out private stablecoins. Roussel sees the relationship as collaborative rather than adversarial.

“I see private stablecoins and CBDCs as more likely to coexist than simply compete,” Roussel suggested. “A CBDC can provide a sovereign form of digital money, but money is only one part of the financial stack. Users and businesses also need wallets, distribution, liquidity, cross-border connectivity, payments, credit, and treasury infrastructure.”

In this dual framework, CBDCs offer a sovereign, base-layer digital unit of account, while private stablecoins and commercial layers drive cross-border connectivity, agile platform integration, and tailored financial products.

“If CBDCs become widely used, they could actually reinforce the broader transition toward programmable digital money,” sayid Roussel. “Ultimately, I think the market will be less about CBDC versus stablecoin and more about how different forms of digital money interact with the financial infrastructure around them.”

Layer 2 Scaling and the Shift to Productive Capital

The mass migration of stablecoin traffic to Layer 2 networks and high-throughput Layer 1 blockchains has drastically compressed transaction costs. With sub-cent, near-instant settlement now a reality, the basic economics of issuing and managing stablecoins are undergoing a fundamental transformation.

When transaction fees drop toward zero, moving money ceases to be the primary revenue driver.

“If the transaction itself becomes almost free, issuers and infrastructure providers cannot rely primarily on transaction fees,” Roussel observed. “They will increasingly compete through distribution, liquidity, financial services, treasury products, and the ability to build useful services around the stablecoin.”

This fundamental shift aligns directly with Frgmnt’s mission of transforming stablecoins from passive transactional tools into active, programmable assets.

“A stablecoin shouldn’t just be a cheap way to move dollars. It can become a programmable financial asset that can move, settle, earn, and interact with financial infrastructure,” Roussel said. “And once the marginal cost of moving that dollar approaches zero, the economic value increasingly comes from what you can build around the dollar rather than from the transaction itself. That’s a very important transition for the industry: from cheaper payments to programmable and productive capital.”

title: Strategy Declares Daily STRC Dividends As Saylor Targets $100 Share Price
summary: TL;DR: Strategy has conditionally declared daily STRC preferred-stock dividends for November 2026. The new cadence remains subject to shareholder approval and is intended to make the security more attractive to investors. Strategy is proposing another adjustment to the financing instruments supporti...
content:
TL;DR: Strategy has conditionally declared daily STRC preferred-stock dividends for November 2026. The new cadence remains subject to shareholder approval and is intended to make the security more attractive to investors.

Strategy is proposing another adjustment to the financing instruments supporting its Bitcoin treasury business, this time seeking approval to pay dividends on its STRC preferred stock every day.

In an October 16 filing, the company outlined conditional daily dividend record dates for November. The announced rate was equivalent to approximately 12% annually, or $1 per preferred share for the month.

The plan depends on amendments that shareholders are due to consider at an October 28 meeting.

A Different Way To Attract Capital

STRC, also known as Stretch, is a variable-rate preferred security developed as part of Strategy’s effort to finance Bitcoin purchases.

Its appeal to investors is linked to recurring income and the company’s attempts to keep the share price close to its $100 reference level.

More frequent distributions could reduce the time between earning and receiving a dividend. That does not automatically increase the total amount paid or guarantee daily compounding.

Strategy has already used STRC-related financing to expand its Bitcoin holdings.

The Costs Still Matter

Preferred financing can raise money without immediately issuing more common shares, but it creates dividend obligations that require ongoing management.

Those costs become particularly important during prolonged weakness in the Bitcoin market.

If shareholders approve the changes and other conditions are met, the new STRC dividend schedule is expected to begin in November. Otherwise, existing arrangements will remain in place.

For investors, the vote offers another indication of how sophisticated Strategy’s capital structure has become as its Bitcoin treasury grows.

Written by the News Desk and edited by Samuel Rae.

title: Bitcoin Price at $81,500 Leaves Bulls and Bears at a Standoff
summary: Bitcoin traded near $81,500 on Oct. 17, 2026, with its technical indicators offering competing signals. Shorter-term moving averages favored sellers, while longer-term averages continued to support buyers. The relative strength index (RSI) stood at 46, and the broader technical rating remained neutr...
content:
Bitcoin traded near $81,500 on Oct. 17, 2026, with its technical indicators offering competing signals. Shorter-term moving averages favored sellers, while longer-term averages continued to support buyers. The relative strength index (RSI) stood at 46, and the broader technical rating remained neutral. With support clustered around $81,000 and resistance extending toward $82,500, bitcoin faces a consequential test of its recent consolidation.

Key Takeaways

  • Bitcoin’s price traded near $81,500 on Oct. 17, with $81,000 support and $82,500 resistance defining the battle.
  • BTC’s oscillators remained largely neutral, while shorter-term moving averages favored sellers.
  • Bitcoin retained bullish longer-term averages, but a break below $80,714 would expose $79,694.

Bitcoin Price Stalls at $81,500 as Short-Term Bears Challenge Longer-Term Bulls

Bitcoin’s price is caught in a rather peculiar technical standoff, trading around $81,500 on Saturday, Oct. 17, 2026, as bearish short-term moving averages clash with a considerably healthier longer-term structure.

With a market capitalization of approximately $1.639 trillion, $13.967 billion in daily trading volume and a 24-hour range stretching from $81,108.80 to $81,733.01, the market has settled into a narrow holding pattern, leaving traders to determine whether the latest consolidation represents the beginnings of a recovery or merely a temporary reprieve before another test of support.

Hourly Chart Shows Buyers Defending Their Ground

The one-hour chart presents a tentative recovery from the recent $80,714 low, with successive higher lows suggesting buyers are attempting to establish a foothold around $81,000. However, declining trading volume complicates that encouraging development, indicating the recovery has yet to attract convincing participation.

Immediate resistance rests between $81,700 and $82,000, where a sustained advance would bring $82,500 into consideration. Conversely, a retreat through $81,000 would expose the earlier hourly low and challenge the modest progress buyers have achieved.

Four-Hour Structure Keeps Sellers in Contention

The four-hour chart offers a less forgiving perspective, showing bitcoin consolidating after its rejection near $84,254. Price action remains concentrated around $81,000 to $81,700, with neither side demonstrating sufficient conviction to establish a decisive directional move. Order-book observations place additional bids toward $80,000, while overhead offers extend into higher price territory.

A recovery above $82,500 would begin repairing the immediate technical picture, although the $83,000 region presents another obstacle. Failure to preserve $81,000 would instead direct attention toward $79,694, an important structural support level.

Daily Chart Reveals a Divided Technical Picture

On the daily chart, bitcoin continues to register lower highs following its earlier advance to $87,374, a pattern consistent with weakening upward momentum. Nevertheless, the broader structure has not surrendered its longer-term technical foundations.

The $80,000 region remains particularly consequential, serving as both a psychological boundary and a nearby technical reference point. Losing that territory would bring $79,694 and potentially $78,000 into focus. Buyers, meanwhile, need to reclaim $83,000 before the daily picture begins looking materially healthier, with $84,254 representing another meaningful resistance barrier.

Oscillators Remain Cautious as Moving Averages Split

The oscillator readings provide little evidence of a decisive shift in momentum. The relative strength index (RSI) stands at 46, indicating neither an overbought nor an oversold condition, while the Stochastic registers 27. The commodity channel index (CCI) sits at negative 116, and the average directional index (ADX) reads 24.

Meanwhile, the moving average convergence divergence (MACD) level of 80 carries a bearish signal, contrasting with positive classifications assigned to momentum and bull bear power. Collectively, eight neutral readings leave directional conviction conspicuously absent.

Moving averages (MAs) tell a more divided story. Bitcoin trades beneath its 10-period exponential moving average (EMA) at $82,343 and 20-period simple moving average (SMA) at $83,405, reinforcing near-term resistance. Yet the 50-period exponential moving average (EMA) at $80,416 and 50-period simple moving average (SMA) at $81,322 remain beneath the market, while the 100- and 200-period averages also retain bullish classifications.

Bull Verdict 🐂Bear Verdict 🐻
Bitcoin bulls need to reclaim $82,500 to demonstrate that buyers are regaining control of the short-term trend. A sustained breakout above $83,000 would strengthen the recovery case and put $84,254 within reach. Holding the $81,000 support region while defending longer-term moving averages would further reinforce the bullish argument and suggest the latest consolidation is laying the groundwork for another upward advance.Bitcoin bears retain an advantage while prices remain beneath the $82,500 resistance barrier. A decisive breakdown below $81,000, followed by a loss of $80,714, would expose $79,694 and potentially the $78,000 region. Persistent selling pressure beneath shorter-term moving averages would strengthen the bearish case, threaten the broader recovery structure and place longer-term technical support under increasingly intense scrutiny.

title: Circle Reveals $819 Million USDC Payouts As Stablecoin Economics Come Under Scrutiny
summary: TL;DR: Circle says it generated roughly $1.4 billion in first-half 2026 revenue while spending $819 million on distribution partners and related costs. The disclosure highlights the expense of building a widely used stablecoin payment network. Circle’s USDC business is generating substantial revenue...
content:
TL;DR: Circle says it generated roughly $1.4 billion in first-half 2026 revenue while spending $819 million on distribution partners and related costs. The disclosure highlights the expense of building a widely used stablecoin payment network.

Circle’s USDC business is generating substantial revenue, but its latest disclosures show how much of that income is needed to support distribution and infrastructure.

The stablecoin issuer reported approximately $1.4 billion of revenue in the first half of 2026. It said around $819 million went to partners and transaction-related costs, while another $473 million supported operational, compliance and technology spending.

That leaves a much smaller proportion of revenue as retained profit than the headline size of USDC might suggest.

The Economics Of A Digital Dollar

Circle holds reserves backing USDC in cash and highly liquid financial instruments. Those assets can produce interest income, creating an important revenue stream for the issuer.

But USDC’s usefulness depends on its presence across exchanges, wallets, payment services and other financial applications.

Those distribution arrangements can be expensive. Coinbase is among Circle’s most important commercial partners, reflecting its role in making the stablecoin accessible to users.

As NewsBTC has previously explained, USDC aims to maintain its value against the dollar while remaining transferable across supported networks.

Competition Raises The Stakes

New stablecoin issuers and conventional financial institutions are entering the market. They will compete not only on the reliability of their reserves but also on distribution, redemption and cost.

Circle’s revenue also depends partly on interest rates. Lower yields on reserves could compress income even if USDC’s circulation remains relatively strong.

The latest figures reveal an important part of the stablecoin business: issuing the digital dollar may be only the first step. The partners enabling people to use it can command a considerable share of the economic value.

Written by the News Desk and edited by Samuel Rae.

title: French Assembly Narrowly Adopts Stablecoin Swap Tax Proposal
summary: If passed, the measure would subject French cryptocurrency holders to a 31.4% capital gains tax each time they exchange a cryptocurrency for a stablecoin. Analysts agree this would prompt French crypto holders to consider alternatives to park their digital assets. France’s National Assembly Adopts C...
content:
If passed, the measure would subject French cryptocurrency holders to a 31.4% capital gains tax each time they exchange a cryptocurrency for a stablecoin. Analysts agree this would prompt French crypto holders to consider alternatives to park their digital assets.

Key Takeaways

  • French lawmakers narrowly passed a proposal to tax crypto-to-stablecoin swaps with capital gains tax.
  • The measure targets a tax loophole, which could limit traders’ ability to park gains tax-free.
  • The controversial rule faces an upcoming Senate vote before potentially taking effect in January 2027.

France’s National Assembly Adopts Crypto-To-Stablecoin Exchange Taxation

France is on the verge of tightening its cryptocurrency regulation framework, putting taxation front and center.

On Friday, as part of the 2027 Finance bill debate, the National Assembly discussed and adopted Amendment I-3898, which proposes taxing crypto-to-stablecoin exchanges with capital gains tax.

Filed by MP Nicolas Sansu and passed by the Finance Committee last week, the amendment passed by a narrow 38-37 vote with 25 abstentions: out of 577, only 100 MPs participated in the vote.

The amendment seeks to plug what French legislators called a regulatory loophole, considering that stablecoins fulfill some functions of money, including making payments and other investments.

Currently, these exchanges are not taxed, which the proposal argues deprives the government of a valuable tax resource that “does not create any new burden,” as the amendment stresses. Nonetheless, the landscape of digital assets in France would change extensively if the proposal reaches law status.

Arbitrage and speculative trading activities would suffer, as traders generally use stablecoins to park earnings to avoid being taxed before exchanging them for fiat currencies. Chainalysis determined that 90% of France’s crypto gains go undeclared, with only 24,000 French taxpayers declaring nearly $427 million in gains for 2024.

Analysts have lamented this development, claiming that French crypto holders will be deprived of a tool to avoid the volatility of the cryptocurrency market, and that stablecoin adoption will be hampered as a result.

The popularity of commodity digital assets such as gold-linked tokens could also rise as French crypto holders rotate into these alternatives to try to mitigate volatility losses. Nonetheless, the solution remains imperfect, as gold also faces high volatility periods.

As the proposal remains controversial and divisive, the Senate might step in and change it or reject it entirely. French media indicates that the government, which remains opposed to this measure, could exclude this amendment or approve the bill’s first iteration without amendments, so the proposal can still change before the budget bill approval.

However, if passed without changes, taxation of crypto-to-stablecoin exchanges will become effective on January 1, 2027, with its delivery to the Senate being decided by vote next Tuesday.

title: Charles Schwab Opens Bitcoin And Ethereum Transfers As Crypto Rollout Expands
summary: TL;DR: Charles Schwab is expanding its direct Bitcoin and Ethereum services, including phased external wallet transfers. The move brings digital asset ownership further into the company’s conventional brokerage experience. Charles Schwab is moving its cryptocurrency service closer to the features cu...
content:
TL;DR: Charles Schwab is expanding its direct Bitcoin and Ethereum services, including phased external wallet transfers. The move brings digital asset ownership further into the company’s conventional brokerage experience.

Charles Schwab is moving its cryptocurrency service closer to the features customers expect from a dedicated digital asset platform.

The brokerage has been rolling out direct Bitcoin and Ethereum trading to eligible clients, and its latest account documentation explains how approved customers can transfer supported assets to and from external wallets.

For Schwab, that is a meaningful step beyond providing market exposure inside an investment account.

Buying Crypto Is Only The Beginning

Brokerage customers increasingly want to decide whether to hold digital assets with a financial institution or move them to another approved custody arrangement.

Schwab’s transfer functionality is being introduced in phases. Users must meet identity verification requirements and may encounter security checks and waiting periods for approved wallet addresses.

The platform also continues to distinguish cryptocurrency from conventional insured bank deposits. The value of Bitcoin and Ethereum is not protected by FDIC insurance merely because the assets are held through a Schwab service.

As NewsBTC reported when Schwab introduced direct crypto trading, the rollout has been deliberately gradual.

Traditional Brokerages Become Serious Rivals

Schwab already has millions of brokerage relationships and well-established infrastructure. Adding cryptocurrency ownership makes those relationships increasingly valuable in a market where digital asset exchanges are competing with conventional financial firms.

The company has also discussed expanding its supported assets beyond Bitcoin and Ethereum.

The wider trend is clear: investors are increasingly being offered cryptocurrency services through the same institutions they use for stocks and other financial products.

The competitive question is no longer simply whether traditional brokerages will support cryptocurrency. It is how much of the customer experience they intend to control.

Written by the News Desk and edited by Samuel Rae.

title: Lopp’s Wrench Attack Map Hits 702 After AI-Assisted Search Work
summary: Bitcoin security expert Jameson Lopp’s archive of physical attacks against cryptocurrency holders has more than doubled to over 700 documented incidents after researcher Pizza Bitcoiner used artificial intelligence (AI)-assisted searches to uncover hundreds of overlooked cases. The expanded records ...
content:
Bitcoin security expert Jameson Lopp’s archive of physical attacks against cryptocurrency holders has more than doubled to over 700 documented incidents after researcher Pizza Bitcoiner used artificial intelligence (AI)-assisted searches to uncover hundreds of overlooked cases.

Key Takeaways

  • Jameson Lopp’s Bitcoin wrench attack archive now documents more than 700 physical attacks.
  • Pizza Bitcoiner’s AI-assisted research uncovered 375 cases missing from Lopp’s earlier records.
  • Pizza Bitcoiner’s database records 31 deaths and approximately $394 million in reported losses.

The expanded records expose a disturbing history of kidnappings, home invasions, and violent robberies, including 31 reported deaths since 2020. The dramatic increase reflects better documentation, not a sudden doubling of attacks.

Criminals don’t need to crack Bitcoin’s cryptography when they can threaten the people holding the keys. Now, AI-assisted detective work has uncovered hundreds of overlooked physical attacks, more than doubling Jameson Lopp’s public archive to over 700 documented cases.

AI Investigation Uncovers Hundreds of Forgotten Bitcoin Attacks

Bitcoin security expert and Casa co-founder Jameson Lopp revealed the dramatic expansion of his physical attack archive on Oct. 16, 2026, crediting researcher Pizza Bitcoiner for uncovering hundreds of incidents previously missing from the records.

Lopp broke the news on X with an announcement that mixed appreciation with a rather grim discovery, stating:

“Good news: the Bitcoin Wrench Attack archive just got a lot more accurate. Bad news: we just doubled the total number of known attacks to over 700. Kudos to Pizza Bitcoiner for finding hundreds of new attack reports via agentic searches.”

The interactive archive now documents approximately 702 incidents dating back to 2014, including home invasions, kidnappings, violent robberies and extortion schemes.

These crimes are known as wrench attacks, a term borrowed from an XKCD comic illustrating how physical intimidation can defeat sophisticated digital security. Rather than hacking a wallet, criminals threaten its owner until the cryptocurrency changes hands.

Pizza Bitcoiner’s AI Search Breaks Open the Records

The breakthrough came from Pizza Bitcoiner, whose separate database documents 670 verified incidents across 72 countries between January 2020 and mid-October 2026. Of those cases, 375 were missing from Lopp’s earlier collection, with approximately 351 subsequently added to his repository.

The investigation employed AI-assisted searches across local-language news outlets, court records and police reports, uncovering incidents that traditional research had overlooked. Pizza Bitcoiner responded to Lopp’s acknowledgment with gratitude and a commitment to keep the investigation running. The researcher wrote:

“You are the one I should be thanking for starting it in the first place.
I’m very happy to help! My pipeline will be running every week, adding new cases and also updating old ones with new evidence. The data will continue to remain available for download.”

Hundreds Held Captive, Millions Stolen and 31 Killed

The expanded dataset paints a disturbing picture of cryptocurrency’s physical security problem. Among 670 documented incidents, 413 involved victims being held against their will, 300 resulted in injuries and 31 ended in deaths. Reported financial losses totaled approximately $394 million across 447 cases with available figures. Annual records climbed from 37 incidents in 2020 to 165 in 2025, with another 134 documented through mid-October 2026.

France has emerged as a prominent hotspot, while the United States also accounts for numerous reported attacks. However, the numbers come with an important qualification. Improved searches and broader language coverage explain some of the increase, meaning the newly discovered cases do not necessarily indicate a comparable rise in actual crime.

Bitcoin’s Digital Defenses Meet a Physical Reality

The findings expose a vulnerability that encryption alone cannot eliminate. Multisignature wallets, geographically separated keys and spending delays can complicate forced transfers, but they cannot guarantee protection against physical violence. Public disclosures of cryptocurrency holdings, compromised personal information and face-to-face transactions can also expose potential victims to targeting.

Neither archive claims to capture every incident. Many attacks go unreported, while others never reach searchable public records. The real shock isn’t that hundreds of new attacks suddenly occurred. It’s that hundreds had already happened, and much of the world never knew.

title: Crypto Giants Feature In $210 Million Political Donations Report As Regulatory Scrutiny Grows
summary: TL;DR: An October 8 Public Citizen report links corporations and individuals benefiting from cancelled federal enforcement actions to approximately $210.5 million in donations and pledges to Trump-aligned political committees. Major cryptocurrency companies feature among the reported contributors. A...
content:
TL;DR: An October 8 Public Citizen report links corporations and individuals benefiting from cancelled federal enforcement actions to approximately $210.5 million in donations and pledges to Trump-aligned political committees. Major cryptocurrency companies feature among the reported contributors.

A report examining corporate political donations and changes to federal enforcement has placed several major cryptocurrency businesses under renewed public scrutiny.

Consumer advocacy organisation Public Citizen said companies and individuals connected to beneficiaries of cancelled or curtailed enforcement actions had contributed or pledged roughly $210.5 million to Trump-aligned political committees.

The research, originally published October 8, includes cryptocurrency firms such as Crypto.com and Gemini. It should not be described as a brand-new October 16 investigation.

The Crypto Industry’s Political Spending

According to the report, Crypto.com-associated contributions included $35 million to MAGA Inc. and another $2 million to a separate Trump-aligned committee.

Public Citizen also examined contributions involving Gemini and the Winklevoss brothers, alongside regulatory matters affecting the exchange.

The watchdog argues that the scale of political spending deserves attention, particularly where companies also benefit from changes in how government agencies pursue enforcement.

But political contributions are not proof of an illegal arrangement. The report does not establish that the named donors purchased specific regulatory decisions.

A Broader Political Debate

The cryptocurrency industry has become increasingly involved in Washington, advocating for clearer legislation and a more predictable business environment.

NewsBTC has previously reported on substantial cryptocurrency political contributions, part of a larger push to influence rules affecting exchanges, stablecoins and token issuers.

Supporters of those efforts argue that previous regulation created unnecessary uncertainty. Critics say large corporate donors may enjoy disproportionate access to policymakers.

Public Citizen’s findings add to that debate while leaving the central legal distinction intact: correlation between donations and enforcement outcomes does not establish corruption.

Written by the News Desk and edited by Samuel Rae.

title: XRP Ledger Nears Oct. 23 Upgrade as Lending Votes Fall Short
summary: The XRP Ledger is heading toward an Oct. 23 software upgrade that fixes a peculiar security flaw, one that could let certain authorized accounts create tokens instead of destroying them. Meanwhile, its long-awaited native lending system remains stuck awaiting approval. XRP Ledger’s Cleanup Upgrade A...
content:
The XRP Ledger is heading toward an Oct. 23 software upgrade that fixes a peculiar security flaw, one that could let certain authorized accounts create tokens instead of destroying them. Meanwhile, its long-awaited native lending system remains stuck awaiting approval.

Key Takeaways

  • XRP Ledger’s fixCleanup3_4_0 targets Oct. 23 activation after securing more than 80% validator support.
  • XRPL’s upgrade closes a loophole that could let PaymentBurn delegates create tokens instead of destroying them.
  • XRP Ledger’s native lending amendments remain below the approval threshold, leaving launch dates uncertain.

XRP Ledger’s Cleanup Upgrade Approaches Activation

The XRP Ledger (XRPL) is preparing to activate fixCleanup3_4_0 at approximately 09:34 UTC on Oct. 23, provided validator support holds above the required 80% threshold. The amendment secured its supermajority on Oct. 9, starting a mandatory two-week countdown. By mid-October, approximately 26 to 29 validators out of 32 to 35 supported the change, according to the supplied XRPSCAN amendment tracking.

There’s a catch. If support slips to 80% or lower before activation, the countdown resets. The amendment must then maintain sufficient backing for another uninterrupted two weeks. Unlike protocol upgrades that introduce new trading products, this one concentrates on fixing existing software behavior. The package, introduced in rippled version 3.4.0, addresses lending infrastructure, automated market makers, token handling, escrow transactions and account permissions.

A Token-Burning Permission Had a Minting Problem

Perhaps the most interesting correction concerns a feature activated Oct. 8 called PermissionDelegationV1_1. That feature allows account owners to give another account limited authority to perform specific actions without surrendering their main account keys. One permission, called Paymentburn, is supposed to let an authorized account destroy certain tokens. Yet a software flaw could produce the opposite result under specific conditions, allowing tokens to be created instead.

Official XRPL documentation warns operators against granting that particular permission until the cleanup amendment activates. The update also corrects how vaults calculate withdrawals, tightens the rules for declaring loans overdue and prevents certain automated market maker transactions from destroying liquidity tokens without returning assets.

For ordinary XRP holders, the changes should be largely invisible. Node operators, however, need compatible software to continue following network consensus after activation.

Native XRP Ledger Lending Still Has No Launch Date

Funnily enough, the cleanup includes several lending-related fixes even though native lending itself hasn’t received approval. The proposed Lending Protocol would allow users to pool assets and fund fixed-term loans through the XRP Ledger. Borrowers wouldn’t necessarily provide collateral, while loan brokers would arrange terms and assess creditworthiness outside the blockchain.

Three separate amendments must activate to deliver the complete lending system. As of Oct. 15-17, the two lending amendments reportedly had approximately 17 to 19 supporting validators, or roughly 53%. The required Singleassetvault amendment had around 19 to 21 supporters. All remained short of the necessary supermajority, leaving their activation dates undetermined.

The distinction is important for anyone watching the upgrade calendar. Oct. 23 could deliver software corrections that make lending infrastructure safer, while the lending system those corrections support remains unavailable. For now, XRPL’s validators appear closer to approving the repairs than the financial product itself.

title: Binance.US Seeks $100 Million Funding Round At $1 Billion Valuation
summary: TL;DR: Binance.US is reportedly seeking up to $100 million from private investors at a proposed valuation of approximately $1 billion. The financing discussions come as the American exchange attempts to rebuild after several difficult years. Binance.US is reportedly pursuing a $100 million fundraisi...
content:
TL;DR: Binance.US is reportedly seeking up to $100 million from private investors at a proposed valuation of approximately $1 billion. The financing discussions come as the American exchange attempts to rebuild after several difficult years.

Binance.US is reportedly pursuing a $100 million fundraising round as it seeks to strengthen its presence in the American cryptocurrency market.

Bloomberg reported on October 15 that the exchange was discussing an investment at a valuation of approximately $1 billion. If completed on those terms, it would represent a sharp reduction from the $4.5 billion valuation attached to its 2022 funding round.

The discussions have not been announced as a closed transaction, and the proposed figures could change.

Rebuilding A Damaged Business

Binance.US once competed aggressively for American cryptocurrency traders but faced major regulatory and operational difficulties.

The Securities and Exchange Commission’s earlier proceedings complicated the company’s relationships with banks and other commercial partners. As NewsBTC covered at the time, those disputes included an emergency application involving assets connected to the platform.

Conditions have since changed, with US regulators adopting a different approach to digital asset businesses. But a friendlier environment alone does not guarantee that customers return.

Fresh funding could support compliance, technology development and new products, while giving Binance.US greater flexibility to compete with established exchanges and brokerages.

What The Valuation Suggests

A proposed $1 billion valuation is not itself a completed market transaction, but it is a reminder of how substantially expectations for cryptocurrency platforms have evolved since 2022.

The next challenge for Binance.US will be demonstrating that investment capital can translate into stronger trading activity and sustainable growth.

For now, the fundraising discussions show renewed ambition rather than a finished recovery.

Written by the News Desk and edited by Samuel Rae.

title: Goldman, Wells Fargo, Morgan Stanley see tokenization as a growth play, not a threat
summary: The largest banks in the world are eyeing new trading opportunities, speeding up payments and a role for advisers as tokenization takes root in Wall Street.
content:
Oct 17, 2026, 1:00 p.m. EDT

3 min read

Summary

  • Goldman Sachs sees tokenization as a way to expand its trading business.
  • Wells Fargo says its tokenized deposit system is already processing cross-border payments in two minutes or less.
  • Morgan Stanley is looking to tokenization to create more demand for wealth management advice as investors gain new ways to move assets.

Tokenization, or the process of bringing financial and real-world assets onto a blockchain, has been generating headlines in recent months, with a growing number of companies saying they’re offering, or planning to offer, versions of equities, bonds and commodities that can be traded around the clock with few, if any, geographic restrictions.

Not surprisingly, Wall Street's biggest banks are also examining the technology, and this week’s third-quarter earnings calls allowed executives the opportunity to voice a clearer picture of where they think the business is headed, though none put a revenue figure on the opportunity.

Goldman Sachs (GS), Wells Fargo (WFC) and Morgan Stanley (MS) focused on different aspects of the process: trading opportunities, money transmission and advisory services.

For Goldman Sachs, it’s all about trading. CEO David Solomon was asked whether tokenization, decentralized finance (DeFi) and prediction markets could eat into the firm's trading revenue. His answer was that they might do the opposite.

Solomon pointed to the shift toward electronic stock trading almost 50 years ago, which once raised similar concerns about the future of Wall Street's trading desks. Goldman adapted to that change and its equities business grew. Tokenization, he said, could follow a similar path.

"The developments are obviously creating more products, greater activity, potentially new clients, broader distribution channels," Solomon said on Tuesday’s call with analysts.

Tokenization, clearing and settlement

The bank has spent years investing in digital asset infrastructure, though perhaps more quietly than most of its competitors. It built GS DAP, its own platform for tokenized assets, as long ago as 2022 and has worked on tokenizing bonds, money market funds and real estate.

In July, the bank participated in a half-day run of a tokenization service from the Depository Trust & Clearing Corporation (DTCC), which handles much of the plumbing behind U.S. securities markets and processes quadrillions of dollars of transactions each year.

Goldman is now looking at ways to use that service on a larger scale, with Solomon claiming tokenization could help cut costs, automate transactions and make assets easier to trade. But he was careful about how much business it represents today.

"I'd say the activity so far is small and at the margin," he said.

Wells Fargo, meanwhile, is already processing cross-border payments using tokenized deposits, with money reaching beneficiary accounts in two minutes or less.

"This is in production, by the way, and it's small volume so far," CFO Michael Santomassimo said.

The bigger opportunity for Wells Fargo may be geographic. Unlike some of its global rivals, the bank doesn't have a large international branch network. Santomassimo said tokenized deposits could help it win more cross-border payments business without having to build that network.

The bank also sees other possible uses for the technology, including tokenized securities, real-world assets and crypto trading for wealth clients. Santomassimo did not say when those services might become available.

For Morgan Stanley, the emphasis is less on moving money and more on what happens when investors can move assets with fewer delays.

While the technology could make it faster and easier to transfer investments, that doesn't mean clients will stop needing advice, CFO Sharon Yeshaya said .

"The tokenized world means it is faster and easier to move assets around, and you will need advice," she said.

Morgan Stanley has been investing in digital capabilities across its wealth management and institutional securities businesses. Yeshaya did not announce a new product, simply identifying tokenization as another opportunity for the firm.

title: Turkey’s Justice Minister Confirms Richard Heart’s Istanbul Bust
summary: Turkish authorities detained HEX founder Richard Heart and four others in Istanbul, uncovering an extraordinary collection of cash, luxury goods, weapons and electronics. The haul included an estimated $7.15 million in cash, six cryptocurrency wallets, and hundreds of designer accessories. Turkey’s ...
content:
Turkish authorities detained HEX founder Richard Heart and four others in Istanbul, uncovering an extraordinary collection of cash, luxury goods, weapons and electronics. The haul included an estimated $7.15 million in cash, six cryptocurrency wallets, and hundreds of designer accessories.

Key Takeaways

  • Turkey’s justice minister confirmed Richard Heart’s Oct. 14 detention alongside four others in Istanbul.
  • Turkish authorities reported seizing $7.15 million in cash, six cold wallets and hundreds of luxury items.
  • Richard Heart faces unresolved Finnish allegations despite the dismissal of his U.S. SEC case in 2025.

Turkey’s Justice Minister Confirms Richard Heart Detention

Turkey’s Justice Minister Akın Gürlek confirmed Saturday, Oct. 17, that Richard James Schueler, better known as Richard Heart, was detained during an Oct. 14 operation in Istanbul’s Beşiktaş district. The announcement marks the first official acknowledgment of the detention and provides considerably more detail than earlier Turkish media reports.

“Richard James Schueler, a U.S. citizen reported to have an INTERPOL red notice issued against him on allegations of perpetrating a $1 billion cryptocurrency fraud in the United States and Finland, was apprehended and taken into custody in Istanbul,” Gürlek stated.

Schueler, the American entrepreneur behind HEX, Pulsechain and Pulsex, was detained alongside his wife. Three additional men, described as his bodyguards, were subsequently apprehended. Investigators searched 15 properties across Beşiktaş, Üsküdar and Sarıyer, coordinating with Turkish police intelligence, financial crime investigators and the country’s National Intelligence Organization.

Millions in Cash, Designer Goods and Weapons Seized

The inventory released by Gürlek reads like an extraordinarily expensive shopping list. Investigators reported recovering approximately $7.15 million in U.S. currency, 160,000 Turkish lira and six cryptocurrency cold wallets, devices used to secure digital assets. Several luxury vehicles were impounded.

The luxury collection was equally extensive. Authorities listed 300 bags, 100 pairs of shoes, 136 pairs of glasses, 28 watches and 97 pieces of jewelry and other valuables. Police also recovered 29 phones, 12 laptops, 11 computer cases, 19 storage drives, 46 USB devices, 19 graphics cards, seven firearms and 1,400 rounds of ammunition.

“Judicial proceedings regarding the suspects and examinations of the seized materials are ongoing,” Gürlek explained. The figures come directly from the minister’s statement. Authorities haven’t disclosed the contents or potential value of the six cold wallets. Heart’s supporters believe Turkey is being unfair and that he would “receive a fairer and more informed process here in the United States.”

Finnish Red Notice Complicates Heart’s Legal Troubles

Schueler’s detention follows an Interpol Red Notice requested by Finland, where authorities have investigated allegations of aggravated tax fraud involving hundreds of millions of euros. Finnish authorities have also previously identified a separate alleged assault involving a minor. Neither allegation constitutes a conviction, and a Red Notice isn’t an international arrest warrant.

Schueler previously prevailed in a separate American regulatory dispute. The U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) sued him in 2023 over alleged unregistered cryptocurrency offerings exceeding $1 billion. A federal judge dismissed that case in February 2025 on jurisdictional grounds, and the SEC declined to amend its complaint.

“We will not allow anyone to view Turkey as a safe harbor for evading justice,” Gürlek declared. “We will continue with determination to protect our country’s security and to further strengthen our international cooperation in combating transnational crimes.”

Five individuals remain subject to judicial proceedings, with no publicly confirmed extradition filing or court disposition. Meanwhile, the contents of those six cryptocurrency wallets remain undisclosed.

title: Coinbase and Marqeta Bring 24/7 Stablecoin Card Spending to Millions of Merchants
summary:
Key Takeaways: Coinbase and Marqeta are taking a stab at stablecoin-based cards. Coinbase infrastructure makes it easy for businesses to finance card programs around the clock. Cardholders are able to
