content:
2026-10-16T21:42:18.687+02:00

Friday, 16/10/2026 | 19:42 GMT by Tanya Chepkova

  • Online tests may show that clients can find the right answers, not that they understand the risks of a leveraged product.
  • Failing a test does not always block a trade: some clients can proceed after a warning.

Retail investors once had to Google the answers to qualify for high-risk CFDs and complex derivatives; generative AI has turned passing those questionnaires into a one-click exercise.

Now, the UK Financial Conduct Authority is preparing to call time on the shortcut, launching a review into how online brokers screen retail clients as chatbots erode the credibility of traditional risk tests.

The Test Does Not Apply to Every Brokerage Account

An FCA-regulated broker should assess clients’ appropriateness before selling them complex or high-risk products.

Depending on the rules and product structure, the assessment can cover CFDs, complex leveraged exchange-traded products, restricted mass-market investments and qualifying crypto assets.

Unlike suitability assessment, an appropriateness test does not determine whether an investment fits the client’s financial position, objectives or wider portfolio.

It asks whether the person understands what they are buying. In some cases, if a client fails the test, a broker can issue a warning and still allow the transaction if the client asks to continue.

Restricted mass-market investments face a higher threshold: the firm must assess the product as appropriate before accepting the order, with waiting periods applying after repeated failed attempts.

Why Passing a Test Does Not Prove Understanding

The regulator asked brokers and other stakeholders whether appropriateness tests still work for people investing without advice. Some of them warned that clients can use online searches and AI to find the right answers without understanding the risks.

In an online assessment, clients can look up answers as questions appear. Generative AI makes that easier than ever. Respondents to the FCA’s consultation warned that a passing score may therefore reflect someone’s ability to find information rather than their understanding of the investment.

This is especially dangerous with leveraged products. A client may correctly define margin even if they don’t understand how losses can grow when a position moves against them. An answer to an isolated question may not reveal that gap.

The test itself also varies between brokers. Firms have considerable freedom over its content: some assess clients’ understanding rigorously, while others treat it as a “tick-box exercise.”

They also differ over which instruments they consider “non-complex” and exempt from testing. Clients buying similar products may therefore face very different checks.

FCA Will Examine Alternatives in 2027

The FCA continues to view appropriateness assessments as an important safeguard and noted that only a small minority of respondents wanted them abolished or replaced.

Instead, the regulator plans to examine how the current model works, the harm created by its weaknesses and the merits of alternative approaches. It expects to begin engaging with brokers, consumer groups and other stakeholders in 2027.

The review may eventually change how brokers design and document their tests, but the FCA has not yet proposed a replacement model or set a timetable for new rules.

Until then, firms remain responsible for ensuring their questionnaires assess understanding rather than merely presenting another obstacle that clients, and now AI, can quickly navigate.

title: Sazmining Now Sells Jack Dorsey’s Proto Immersion Hashboards
summary:
Bitcoin Magazine

Sazmining Now Sells Jack Dorsey’s Proto Immersion Hashboards 
Block’s Proto mining hashboards are now available on Sazmining’s mining-as-a-service platform. 
This post Sazmining Now Sells Jack Dorsey’s Proto Immersion Hashboards  first appeared on Bitcoin Magazine and is written by...
content:
Bitcoin mining just got a lower barrier to entry. 

Sazmining announced Thursday that it is now selling Proto’s immersion hashboards directly to individual and institutional buyers through its mining-as-a-service platform. Previously, the hardware was mostly in the hands of large-scale operators.

Each hashboard delivers roughly 200 TH at around 15 J/TH, and buyers own them outright while Sazmining handles deployment, monitoring and maintenance at a US facility. Mining rewards go straight to the owner’s wallet.

The move follows a multi-megawatt supply deal between Sazmining and Proto — the bitcoin mining arm of Jack Dorsey’s Block (NYSE: XYZ) — which both companies expect to expand as demand grows.

“Because of our aligned-incentive model, Sazmining only earns when we produce bitcoin for our clients,” said Kent Halliburton, CEO and co-founder of Sazmining. 

He also pitched mining as a form of bitcoin acquisition diversification: rather than paying the market price on the day of purchase, a miner’s costs are spread across the machine’s working life.

Wyoming-based Sazmining, founded in 2018, operates renewable-powered facilities across the US, Paraguay, and Norway. It says its fleet runs more than 20 percentage points ahead of the Bitcoin network’s carbon-free share.

Proto is Jack Dorsey’s Block’s bitcoin mining play. The Twitter founder has spent years arguing bitcoin is the foundation of “a more open financial system,” funding everything from Cash App’s buy-and-send rails to the Bitkey self-custody wallet, and he framed mining as the obvious missing piece back in 2021: “Bitcoin mining should be as easy as plugging a rig into a power source.” 

Block formally announced it was building an open bitcoin mining system in January 2022, with the stated aim of making mining “more distributed and efficient.”

Mathew Di Salvo

Mathew is a reporter who's covered the space since 2019, reporting on everything from Salvadoran president Nayib Bukele's Bitcoin bet to crypto exchange FTX's bankruptcy.

title: Hot Inflation Data Puts Bitcoin Under Pressure, but ‘Difficult’ Isn’t ‘Bearish’: CoinShares
summary:
Bitcoin Magazine

Hot Inflation Data Puts Bitcoin Under Pressure, but ‘Difficult’ Isn’t ‘Bearish’: CoinShares
Bitcoin is still reacting to weekly data but long-term investors shouldn’t be worried, according to the European asset manager. 
This post Hot Inflation Data Puts Bitcoin Under Pressure, but...
content:
Bitcoin’s price has dropped this week as new inflation data has come in hot. 

But while the largest cryptocurrency’s near-term setup is difficult, it’s not “fundamentally bearish,” according to European asset manager CoinShares’ Head of Research, James Butterfill. 

In a report Friday, the analyst said that bitcoin’s near-term challenge stems from a macro environment that’s caught in an awkward middle ground: inflation is too elevated for the Fed to ease up, while the economy is too resilient to force a policy pivot. 

“Bitcoin and the broader digital asset market have moved lower on the resulting hawkish repricing, a reminder of how sensitive Bitcoin remains to monetary policy over short horizons,” he wrote. 

Bitcoin’s price recently stood at $81,473, down 2% over a seven-day period. 

The price of the leading cryptocurrency dropped Wednesday after data showed that U.S. consumer prices shot up more than expected in September. 

Then, on Thursday, the Labor Department’s Bureau of Labor Statistics said that U.S. producer prices rose in September at the fastest pace in more than four years. 

This has weighed on bitcoin’s price because higher inflation means the Federal Reserve may hike interest rates. Higher borrowing costs can restrict the liquidity the digital coin needs to rally. 

The Federal Reserve hiked rates in September and will meet at the end of this month. 

But Butterfill added that investors should be patient and advised investors to instead think in the long-term and not react to any single weekly data point. 

“For investors, that argues for reading the coming weeks as a data-driven range rather than a trend, and for sizing digital asset exposure against a strategic allocation rather than against this week’s print,” he wrote. 

Bitcoin spent the first half of 2026 in a bear market but had its best quarter in years after surging in August and September. Analysts have now said the leading cryptocurrency is now back in a bull market after trading above its 365-day moving average. 

Mathew Di Salvo

Mathew is a reporter who's covered the space since 2019, reporting on everything from Salvadoran president Nayib Bukele's Bitcoin bet to crypto exchange FTX's bankruptcy.

title: Canada Tightens Prediction Market Rules, Banning Brokers from Displaying Sports Contracts
summary:
Canadian brokers offering event contracts must now keep markets they cannot offer out of clients’ sight, not just block trades in them. 
The Canadian Investment Regulatory Organization (CIRO) has extended its restrictions to how prediction markets appear in broker apps and promotions.
London's tradi...
content:
2026-10-16T20:01:00.000+02:00

Friday, 16/10/2026 | 18:01 GMT by Tanya Chepkova

  • Canadian brokers must keep ineligible event contracts out of search results, recommendations and marketing, even when trading is blocked.
  • Wealthsimple’s promotional page still shows hypothetical OpenAI IPO and Apple product questions.

Canadian brokers offering event contracts must now keep markets they cannot offer out of clients’ sight, not just block trades in them.

The Canadian Investment Regulatory Organization (CIRO) has extended its restrictions to how prediction markets appear in broker apps and promotions.

London's trading industry is coming home!

The updated requirements, published on 16 October, also explicitly prohibit sports and entertainment contracts. Brokers distributing products from US prediction exchanges will therefore need a separate Canadian selection of markets.

Brokers Must Filter the Entire Product Experience

CIRO says dealers must keep unavailable contracts out of search results, recommendations and marketing, even when clients cannot trade them. Sending clients to those markets through links to third-party sites is also prohibited.

The regulator says showing such contracts could give clients the impression that they are authorised in Canada. A broker connected to a larger US exchange must therefore filter markets before they reach its Canadian interface.

The rule may also affect how brokers advertise prediction markets.

Wealthsimple’s Predict page still displays illustrative questions about an OpenAI IPO and a foldable Apple phone. Those examples do not mean the contracts are available to trade, but Wealthsimple may need to review whether they can remain in Canadian-facing marketing.

Economic and Financial Contracts Remain Available

CIRO continues to permit selected contracts tied to economic data, environmental measurements and financial indicators. Eligibility depends on an objective way to determine the outcome, such as an official statistic or a recognised market benchmark.

The existing minimum maturity of 30 days and prohibition on leverage also remain in place. CIRO set out those conditions in its earlier guidance.

CIRO had already said in August that sports and entertainment contracts did not belong within the securities-regulated offering it authorised for dealers. The latest notice makes the restriction explicit and extends it to the way those markets are presented to clients.

Two Brokers Currently Serve the Canadian Market

Interactive Brokers Canada launched event contracts in April 2025, and became the first dealer authorised to offer those products in the country. Its Forecast Contracts trade through ForecastEx, the CFTC-regulated exchange owned by Interactive Brokers.

Wealthsimple later received authorisation and now distributes selected Kalshi contracts through its separate Predict app. Its Canadian offering is limited to approved financial, economic and climate-related markets.

As ForecastEx and Kalshi add contracts, both brokers will have to assess each new market before it enters their Canadian product feeds. Keeping an ineligible contract off the trading screen is no longer enough if clients can still encounter it elsewhere.

title: Crypto PACs escalate spending against Sherrod Brown in Ohio Senate race
summary: At least two industry-aligned PACs have poured more than $52 million into opposing Sherrod Brown’s return to the Senate.
content:
Affiliates of the Fairshake political action committee (PAC), largely funded by Coinbase and Ripple Labs, have increased their initially announced expenditures by more than 50% in what could be a key race for control of Congress in 2026.

According to Thursday filings with the Federal Election Commission (FEC), the Fairshake affiliate Defend American Jobs — a group that supports Republican candidates in primaries and elections — spent $46.6 million on media opposing former lawmaker Sherrod Brown and supporting Republican incumbent Jon Husted in Ohio’s Senate race for the 2026 midterms. The spending marked a sharp increase over what Fairshake said in September it initially planned to spend opposing Brown’s return to the Senate: $30 million.

“I’ve spent my career taking on Wall Street, taking on big pharma, taking on big oil and been successful in many cases,” said Brown in an interview aired Friday on Pod Save America, addressing the attack ads funded by the crypto industry, adding:

“Jon Husted is their boy [...] They know he’s their guy, they know I’m going to hold him accountable and I guess it’s a perfect storm, so they spend literally tens and tens of millions of dollars.”

With just under three weeks until the US election, early voting has already been underway for 10 days in Ohio. Notably, Fairshake’s affiliate was not the only crypto-aligned PAC to ramp up spending as Ohio voters cast their ballots. The Digital Freedom Fund, a Super PAC created by Gemini co-founders Tyler and Cameron Winklevoss, reported about $3 million in ad spending this week to oppose Brown and support Husted, bringing the group’s total media purchases in the Ohio race to more than $5.9 million.

Fairshake’s expenditures have already exceeded its efforts in 2024, when the PAC spent $41 million supporting Republican Bernie Moreno and opposing Brown, who was running for reelection to the Senate at the time. The Democratic lawmaker chaired the Senate Banking Committee and was one of the more outspoken voices challenging laws and policies favored by the crypto industry while serving in Congress.

Related: Vivek Ramaswamy’s gubernatorial run lacks the crypto rhetoric of his presidential bid

The Ohio race isn’t Fairshake’s only focus with the midterm elections looming. Defend American Jobs reported spending more than $6.7 million to oppose Independent candidate Dan Osborn in Nebraska’s Senate race. Osborn is running against Republican Pete Ricketts, who voted in favor of the Digital Asset Market Clarity Act and the Guiding and Establishing National Innovation for US Stablecoins Act while in office.

Cointelegraph reached out to Fairshake and Husted’s campaign for comment but did not receive an immediate response.

How could the 2026 elections shape US crypto laws and policy?

Fairshake has been open about its intention to “back pro-crypto candidates” in 2026 as part of a goal to fill the next session of Congress with lawmakers supportive of policies favored by the industry. The PAC reported in January that it held $193 million in cash on hand ahead of the elections.

Beyond PACs like Fairshake and Digital Freedom Fund, other groups aligned with crypto interests have already tried to influence 2026 voters. The Fellowship committee, backed by Cantor Fitzgerald and Anchorage Digital, reported spending more than $11 million between August 2025 and August 2026, largely on media supporting House and Senate candidates.

title: Stablecoin remittances cost 84% less than traditional transfers, report finds
summary: Borderless.xyz data shows major savings on cross-border business payments, with stablecoin transfers also settling faster than traditional international bank wires.
content:
Stablecoin-funded remittances continue to offer substantial cost savings over traditional money transfers, particularly in emerging markets, reinforcing one of the leading use cases for digital dollars as payment activity grows.

According to a new third-quarter report from Borderless.xyz, a stablecoin payments network, sending a $200 remittance through stablecoin-funded payment rails costs a median of 1%, or $2, compared with 6.36%, or $12.72, for traditional remittances, based on World Bank data.

The difference makes stablecoin-funded remittances roughly 84% cheaper, although the comparison uses Borderless’s third-quarter 2026 pricing and World Bank figures from the same period in 2025.

The savings are also substantial across emerging markets. In Sub-Saharan Africa, stablecoin-funded remittances cost 2.9%, compared with 8.46% for traditional transfers. In Latin America, the costs are 1.25% and 5.64%, respectively.

Business payments made through stablecoins are also significantly cheaper, according to the report. A $10,000 stablecoin-funded transfer to the eurozone costs as little as $26 when routed through the lowest-cost provider, compared with $52 across all corridors at the median provider.

By comparison, a traditional international bank wire costs between $135 and $150 for the same amount, including transfer fees and an assumed 1% foreign-exchange margin.

Stablecoins offer significant cost savings on larger business transactions. Source: Borderless.xyz

Related: Mastercard brings stablecoin balances into traditional banking and card payments

Stablecoin payouts settle in minutes, but reliability varies

Beyond cost savings, the Borderless report found that stablecoin-funded payments can reach recipients’ local bank accounts in minutes, depending on the payment network used.

In Brazil, payouts through the PIX network settled in a median of two minutes during the third quarter, while Mexico’s SPEI network took three minutes. Colombia’s PSE network also recorded a median settlement time of two minutes.

By comparison, traditional SWIFT transfers typically settled the next business day, with the slowest 10% taking three business days.

However, payment completion rates varied considerably. Mexico’s SPEI network successfully completed 98.6% of payouts, followed by Brazil’s PIX at 97.8%. Colombia’s PSE network completed 79%, while Costa Rica’s SINPE recorded a completion rate of just 73%.

The findings come as stablecoin transaction activity continues to grow. Standard Chartered recently highlighted rising transaction volumes despite relatively flat growth in the overall stablecoin market capitalization this year. The bank expects the market to reach $2 trillion by 2030, two years later than its previous forecast.

title: Grayscale Opens 3 Crypto Funds on Republic With $2,500 Minimum for Eligible Investors
summary:
Key Takeaways: Grayscale has introduced three crypto-investment products to Republic. A minimum investment of $2,500 is required for those who are eligible, and able to invest as accredited investors. The
The post Grayscale Opens 3 Crypto Funds on Republic With $2,500 Minimum for Eligible Investors ...
content:
Key Takeaways:

  • Grayscale has introduced three crypto-investment products to Republic.
  • A minimum investment of $2,500 is required for those who are eligible, and able to invest as accredited investors.
  • The money primarily goes towards DeFi, decentralized AI, and onchain data infrastructure.

Grayscale and Republic have joined forces to increase adoption of several digital asset investment solutions covering some of crypto’s newsworthy segments.

Excited to partner with @Grayscale to expand investor access on three innovative funds

— Republic (@joinrepublic) October 15, 2026

Through the investment platform the Grayscale DeFi Fund, Grayscale Decentralized AI Fund and Grayscale Data Network Trust are now available to eligible accredited investors.

  • Grayscale Brings Three Crypto Strategies to Republic
    • DATA Trust Targets AI Training Infrastructure
    • $2,500 Minimum Opens Earlier Access
    • Grayscale Expands Beyond Single-Asset Crypto Exposure

Grayscale Brings Three Crypto Strategies to Republic

The release introduces investors to the world of digital assets’ market, without putting all their eggs in one basket. Grayscale DeFi Fund is based on a market-cap-weighted index of decentralized finance protocols engaged in lending, trading, and asset-management.

We’re excited to announce a partnership with @joinrepublic to expand access to Grayscale investment products for eligible investors.

Grayscale products to be available on the Republic platform are:

• Grayscale DeFi Fund: exposure to a basket of leading DeFi protocols
$UNI, $AAVE, $ONDO, $ENA, $CRV, $LDO

• Grayscale Decentralized AI Fund: exposure to protocols operating at the intersection of blockchain and AI
$NEAR, $TAO, $RENDER, $FIL

• Grayscale Data Network Trust: exposure to $DATA, the native token of the DATA Network.

Visit the landing page on Republic to learn more: https://t.co/G16O6hRB3i

— Grayscale (@Grayscale) October 15, 2026

It presents several massive DeFi ecosystems in a single product, such as UNI, AAVE, ONDO, ENA, CRV and LDO.

The Grayscale Decentralized AI Fund is focused on protocols that exist in the intersection of blockchain and artificial intelligence. It has stakes in projects from decentralized computing, storage and AI infrastructure including NEAR, TAO, RENDER and FIL.

Read More: Grayscale’s Zcash ETF Debuts on NYSE Arca, Opening Direct ZEC Exposure to Investors

DATA Trust Targets AI Training Infrastructure

The third product is the Grayscale Data Network Trust, which is focused on the native token of the DATA Network, that same name, “DATA”. According to Grayscale, the network is an AI training infrastructure that pulls data from the same source, verifies, and issues the licenses for training AI models.

This builds an onchain log of data provenance, offers licensing conditions and compensation for rights holders and contributors, and makes the product focus specific, as opposed to the broad range of DeFi and AI funds.

Read More: Vitalik Warns AI Math Could Threaten Crypto Keys Before Quantum Computing Arrives

$2,500 Minimum Opens Earlier Access

Eligible users must invest at least $2,500 of money to invest with Republic, the co-CEO of the organisation said.

The partnership aims to provide more investors than ever before with the chance to be the first to access these products during an earlier development phase typically more open to institutions.

Grayscale CEO Peter Mintzberg indicated that the company evinces the most interesting areas for activity in the digital asset economy include DeFi, decentralized AI, and onchain data infrastructure.

Some of the most compelling opportunities in digital assets are in DeFi, decentralized AI, and onchain data infrastructure.

We’ve spent more than a decade pioneering products and strategies that offer investors exposure to the digital assets ecosystem.

Our partnership with @joinrepublic gives more eligible investors access to the most innovative areas of the fast-growing digital economy.

— Peter Mintzberg (@PeterMintzberg) October 15, 2026

Grayscale Expands Beyond Single-Asset Crypto Exposure

The Republic partnership represents Grayscale’s continued efforts to diversify its flagship crypto product offerings.

The new distribution channel does not just aim at providing exposure to Bitcoin or Ethereum, but rather offers eligible investors exposure to thematic baskets of decentralized finance and artificial intelligence (AI) related crypto infrastructure assets.

These products continue to be private placement securities and are offered to only qualified and accredited investors.

The investments are also highly speculative, liquid and carry the risk of total loss, and are very different from freely traded spot crypto products, according to Grayscale.

title: OKX Marketing Chief Haider Rafique Steps Back After Seven Years at Crypto Exchange
summary:
Key Takeaways: After nearly seven years at OKX, Haider Rafique has decided to step aside due to family and various personal reasons. He played a key role in building the
The post OKX Marketing Chief Haider Rafique Steps Back After Seven Years at Crypto Exchange appeared first on CryptoNinjas.
content:
Key Takeaways:

  • After nearly seven years at OKX, Haider Rafique has decided to step aside due to family and various personal reasons.
  • He played a key role in building the exchange’s global brand and in its increasing visibility via key sports and entertainment deals.
  • Due to the increasing institutional engagement for OKX and the company’s ambition to bridge the gap between crypto and traditional finance, his exit is happening now.

Haider Rafique, OKX’s global managing partner and chief marketing officer, announced that he is stepping back from his position after nearly seven years with the crypto exchange. The announcement marks a change for one of the executives closely associated with OKX’s brand development and international profile.

After almost seven years at @OKX, I am stepping back from my role to take a meaningful break, focus on my family and personal priorities, and make space for what comes next.

It has been an incredible privilege to help build the @OKX brand and see its growth. I am deeply grateful to Star Xu @star_okx for his trust, partnership, and the opportunities he created for all of us.

And thank you to every OKX employee I have had the privilege to work alongside. I am proud of what we built together and excited to see the company continue to grow.

This is not goodbye. It is simply the next chapter.

— haider (@Haider) October 16, 2026

On the social media platform X, Rafique revealed that he would like to take a meaningful break and spend time with his family and some personal priorities before having any idea of what is in the next steps.

He further shared his thoughts on the exchange, thanking its founder Star Xu for his trust and collaboration. Sitting alongside the employees, Rafique expressed his gratitude and was proud of the team that he has formed.

He made this transition a message, and not a final good-bye. He didn’t fill in the void during the break with an announcement of a new position or details of his plans. According to reports published on October 16, his departure is expected by the end of 2026. But there was no final working date announced for the public.

Read More: Abstract to Shut Down Dec. 15 After Consumer Crypto Model Fails to Scale

Seven Years of Building the OKX Brand

Rafique came aboard when crypto exchanges were vying with each other to attract some of the trading community away from the masses. His contributions went beyond merely creating marketing campaigns, ranging from brand positioning to gaining international exposure and aligning with crypto-escrow organizations.

From Rebranding to Global Partnerships

He is also involved in the re-brand initiative from OKEx to OKX, which aims to align the company with its wider branding as a digital asset platform.

OKX also established itself in the traditional sports and entertainment industries via science collaborations with Manchester City, the McLaren Formula 1 team and the Tribeca Festival. These partnerships provided those exchanges with access to audiences they wouldn’t have otherwise.

These kinds of agreements have grown to be a vital component of crypto organizations’ strategies for making their brands visible. In addition to product and technology, visibility and public trust can shape the competition between exchanges in various markets.

OKX Expands Its Institutional Crypto Strategy

Rafique said this comes during a crucial time for OKX’s institutional operations. In March 2026, Intercontinental Exchange, the parent company of the New York Stock Exchange, is reported to have invested around $200 million in OKX at a valuation of around $25 billion.

The exchange has also been working on integrating digital currencies with conventional financial services. Circle, Ripple, Qube Research & Technologies and Standard Chartered’s SC Ventures were reportedly late to the party in October, extending the round.

title: Deutsche Bank To Debut Bitcoin Custody Within Weeks: Report
summary:
Bitcoin Magazine

Deutsche Bank To Debut Bitcoin Custody Within Weeks: Report
The German lender is moving fast with its crypto custody service. 
This post Deutsche Bank To Debut Bitcoin Custody Within Weeks: Report first appeared on Bitcoin Magazine and is written by Mathew Di Salvo.
content:
German multinational Deutsche Bank is just weeks away from its crypto custody service, according to reports. 

The lender — which is Germany’s biggest — also plans to expand the custody platform into Asia next year, according to a Friday Reuters report, which quoted its corporate banking chief. 

Top banks worldwide are debuting or planning to debut crypto custody services, with BNY Mellon, State Street, Standard Chartered, U.S. Bank, and Citigroup all committing to direct crypto custody over the past 18 months.

Deutsche Bank first officially announced plans to debut a bitcoin custody service for European corporate and institutional clients in September, with the German multinational at the time saying service was subject to the completion of the applicable regulatory timeline.

Friday’s report added that the service will support custody of major ⁠cryptocurrencies such as bitcoin before moving to services that help clients move money into and out of ⁠stablecoins.

Gerald Podobnik, co-head of the corporate ⁠bank, was quoted by Reuters saying that the financial system will need to “offer tokenized or blockchain solutions.” 

A number of top banks have started using the technology that powers bitcoin, the blockchain, for their own products in recent years. 

Stablecoins and tokenization in particular have become a hot topic as traditional financial firms aim to accelerate certain services. 

Crypto custody is often a starting point for banks moving into the digital asset space. BNY Mellon in 2022 became the first major U.S. bank to offer digital asset custody services.  

Banks like Citi and Standard Chartered have this year debuted or announced plans for bitcoin custody around the world.

title: MSCI To Move Forward With Proposal That Could Exclude Strategy From Index
summary:
Bitcoin Magazine

MSCI To Move Forward With Proposal That Could Exclude Strategy From Index
MSCI has adopted new rules that could push Bitcoin treasury Strategy out of its global equity benchmarks. 
This post MSCI To Move Forward With Proposal That Could Exclude Strategy From Index first appeared on...
content:
Morgan Stanley Capital International is moving ahead with a proposal that could remove bitcoin juggernaut Strategy from its global equity benchmarks. 

The index maker said Thursday that it “will implement the proposal to define and classify non-operating companies as ineligible for inclusion in the MSCI Global Investable Market Indexes.” 

Bitcoin treasury Strategy previously blasted the idea, calling it “misguided” and “flawed.” 

“MSCI will implement the proposal to define and classify non-operating companies as ineligible for inclusion in the MSCI Global Investable Market Indexes, as set out in the consultation announced on August 3, 2026, with minor modifications,” the statement read. 

“The changes will be implemented as part of the November 2026 Index Review, which will take effect as of the close of November 30, 2026.”

MSCI’s decision won’t immediately remove Strategy from its Global Investable Market Indexes but future tests could end up excluding the company from the index. 

If Strategy does get removed from the index, it would mean that fewer institutional investors can or will hold the stock. 

Strategy did not immediately comment on the MSCI’s decision. The company said of the proposal in August: “Bitcoin doesn’t need MSCI. Neither does Strategy.”

MSCI in 2025 proposed excluding from its indices all companies whose digital-asset holdings represent 50% or more of total assets. 

Strategy — formerly MicroStrategy — is an enterprise software company that pivoted to buying and holding bitcoin in 2020. 

It first bought the cryptocurrency to protect shareholders but has since aggressively bought the asset and is now the largest corporate holder of the cryptocurrency, with 848,250 bitcoins worth $69.2 billion at today’s prices. 

Investors can buy Strategy’s Nasdaq-listed stock (MSTR) to get heightened exposure to bitcoin’s performance. 

Nasdaq-listed Strategy’s shares were trading over 6% lower on Friday.

title: Episode Six Launches Real-Time Stablecoin Backing Checks Across 50+ Global Markets
summary:
Key Takeaways: As part of Episode Six, it has introduced Verified Backing for bank-issued stablecoins and tokenized deposits. The system checks backing at issuance and redemption, not only after transactions.
The post Episode Six Launches Real-Time Stablecoin Backing Checks Across 50+ Global Markets...
content:
Key Takeaways:

  • As part of Episode Six, it has introduced Verified Backing for bank-issued stablecoins and tokenized deposits.
  • The system checks backing at issuance and redemption, not only after transactions.
  • Available in 50+ markets, Episode Six operates worldwide.

With its E6 Token Control Ledger, episode Six has added a real-time verification layer for banks releasing stablecoins and tokenization deposits. Verified Backing is a new capability intended to ensure that a token provides backing upon issuance, and upon subsequent redemption by a customer.

  • Episode Six Checks Stablecoins at Two Critical Moments
  • Checks Continue Even After Tokens Move Across Wallets and Chains
    • Verified Backing Targets Stablecoin Redemption Risk
    • Episode Six Expands Tokenized Banking Infrastructure

Episode Six Checks Stablecoins at Two Critical Moments

Verified Backing works at the issuance and redemption, the two areas in which banks may have the highest risk of using tokenized money.

Before a bank creates a supported stablecoin or tokenized deposit, the system verifies that the required backing has been recorded. It will involve a validation check to ensure at redemption that the token has not been cashed out already, and that the bank’s ledger bears its support.

Episode Six situates it in one that challenges and moves beyond the practice of traditional reconciliation where inconsistencies are only discovered after transactions.

Read More: MoneyGram Launches Stablecoin Card in Colombia, Bringing Crypto Payments to 60M Users

Checks Continue Even After Tokens Move Across Wallets and Chains

The verification process runs inside the issuing bank’s E6 Token Control Ledger. Even if a token passes through several wallets or blockchain networks before it comes back to the bank, episode Six will apply the redemption check.

This provides the issuing institution with a more complete record on the bank side, with which to check the status of the token, as opposed to just after issuance.

Verified Backing Targets Stablecoin Redemption Risk

An important issue about banks that issue tokenized money is, does an asset presented for a redemption amount correspond with a valid outstanding obligation?

It’s not just the question of whether tokens were legitimate at creation, it’s about whether they are legitimate at redemption, said Episode Six APAC Managing Director, Daryn Griggs.

Verified Backing is meant to assist banks in answering that question in real time by verifying the status of the token and the validated backing before money leaves the bank’s vaults.

Read More: 37 European Banks Bring Euro Stablecoin to Ethereum in $300B Market Shake-Up

Episode Six Expands Tokenized Banking Infrastructure

Verified Backing will be added to the Episode Six Token Control Ledger for users in the markets that Episode Six is available in.

The company offers card issuing and ledger infrastructure across over 50 countries across millions of accounts and billions of payment transactions around the world.

The feature could be extended to tokens or tokenized deposits issued by a bank and enter their supported alphabetic stablecoin, says Episode Six.

The launch follows a trend toward an infrastructure that allows banks to create and oversee the tokenization of money, all while retaining the ability to directly oversee backing, redemption and internal records.

title: CySEC Discloses €100,000 TitanEdge Fine after CFD Broker Stops Operations
summary:
CySEC disclosed the penalty two weeks after Titanedge ceased providing investment services and while the regulator was considering the company’s voluntary licence surrender. 
The  Cyprus Securities and Exchange Commission (CySEC) published the announcement on 16 October, however, the enforcement act...
content:
2026-10-16T18:10:00.000+02:00

Friday, 16/10/2026 | 16:10 GMT by Tanya Chepkova

  • CySEC penalised Titanedge for unauthorised investment advice, inadequate compliance procedures and misleading client communications.
  • The decision covers conduct from 2023–2024, although it was disclosed after TitanEdge stopped offering services.

CySEC disclosed the penalty two weeks after Titanedge ceased providing investment services and while the regulator was considering the company’s voluntary licence surrender.

The Cyprus Securities and Exchange Commission (CySEC) published the announcement on 16 October, however, the enforcement action relates to conduct between 2023 and 2024 and was taken before the broker announced its closure.

Three Compliance Failures Cost €100,000

CySEC divided the penalty into three parts, according to its decision.

€30,000 fine was imposed because Titanedge regularly provided investment advice without holding the necessary authorisation. Although the company was licensed as a Cyprus Investment Firm, investment advice was not among the services covered by that licence.

A further €30,000 penalty concerned inadequate internal policies and procedures. CySEC said the company had failed to maintain systems sufficient to ensure ongoing compliance with its regulatory obligations.

The remaining €40,000 related to information supplied to existing and potential clients, including marketing communications. According to the regulator, the company did not ensure that all such material was fair, clear and not misleading.

CySEC considered the case at meetings in October 2025 and July 2026 before publishing the outcome.

Clients Were Told to Close Positions

Titanedge announced that it would discontinue its investment and ancillary services on 14 September. Clients were asked to close open positions, request the withdrawal of available funds and complete any outstanding verification requirements.

The company warned that positions remaining open on 1 October could be closed at the best available market price. Any positive balance would then be returned to the client’s designated bank account, subject to the applicable requirements.

Titanedge also said it intended to renounce its CIF licence, but the surrender is not yet complete: CySEC’s register lists licence 405/21 as under examination for voluntary renunciation.

Titanedge Faced an Earlier CySEC Case

This is not the broker’s first regulatory penalty. In December 2023, Titanedge reached a €90,000 settlement with CySEC over possible violations involving client communications and general conduct requirements between October 2022 and July 2023.

The company paid that amount as part of the settlement. The new fine brings Titanedge’s publicly announced CySEC penalties and settlements to €190,000.

Its business is winding down, but the latest decision shows that ending operations does not prevent the regulator from completing enforcement work covering earlier conduct.

title: Mastercard Taps 17B Endpoints With BVNK Stablecoin Platform Across 200+ Markets
summary:
Key Takeaways: Global Money Platform For Fiat and Stablecoin Payment by Mastercard and BVNK. Mastercard Move links to 17B+ devices globally. The plan is to cover 40+ blockbuster currencies by
The post Mastercard Taps 17B Endpoints With BVNK Stablecoin Platform Across 200+ Markets appeared first on C...
content:
Key Takeaways:

  • Global Money Platform For Fiat and Stablecoin Payment by Mastercard and BVNK.
  • Mastercard Move links to 17B+ devices globally.
  • The plan is to cover 40+ blockbuster currencies by 2027 as well as 200+ markets.

Stablecoins will gain more ground in real-world payments services through stablecoin infrastructure firm BVNK’s partnership with Mastercard and the Global Money Platform service introduced by the latter in August 2026.

The platform offers a single infrastructure layer to banks, fintechs and enterprises to store, convert, send and spend both traditional and stable currency.

  • Mastercard Combines Fiat and Stablecoins in One API
  • Mastercard Move Opens Access to 17 Billion Endpoints
    • Nuvei, Marqeta and Three More Firms Join Early Rollout
    • Mastercard Builds Toward a Multi-Money Payment System

Mastercard Combines Fiat and Stablecoins in One API

Global Money Platform’s core feature is a multi-currency wallet, where stablecoins and fiat currencies differ and go side by side.

There is a single API to enable businesses to switch between the two rather than having to buy separate services for accounts, blockchain infrastructure, settlement and payments.

Stablecoins linked cards and local bank payouts and treasury are also among its features. These functions can be integrated in-platform in the company’s products and sold as part of a company’s brand.

The solution can help save multiple vendors, accounts and pre-funded balances for enterprises across multiple nations, Mastercard says.

Read More: 37 European Banks Bring Euro Stablecoin to Ethereum in $300B Market Shake-Up

Mastercard Move Opens Access to 17 Billion Endpoints

Global Money Platform is directly linked to Mastercard Move, Mastercard’s global money movement infrastructure that spans to over 17 billion endpoints.

This enables businesses to direct local-currency payments straight to the recipients bank accounts without the need to balance with stablecoins. Mastercard is looking forward to growth in the service with a targeted expansion to over 40 currencies in more than 200 countries and territories by 2027.

Stablecoin balances will also be available to use on Mastercard’s worldwide acceptance network, including hundreds of millions of merchants’ engagement points. Platform issuing is anticipated to be offered in over 130 countries.

Nuvei, Marqeta and Three More Firms Join Early Rollout

Alongside Ontop, Bolt Group and Almond FinTech, Nuvei and Marqeta are among the first ones to be getting ready to integrate with Global Money Platform. The integration will give their users the ability to transfer seamlessly between traditional and stablecoins and benefit from existing payment and banking options.

Mastercard’s entry marks a step bigger than just making transactions possible for the stablecoin company. Now the company is offering services which could be embedded in products of other financial firms.

Mastercard Builds Toward a Multi-Money Payment System

Global Money Platform is a platform built on a modular approach including send, receive, convert, store, spend and earn. The customer can start using just the services he or she requires and later upgrade to other services as desired.

Not only is this, but Mastercard is also looking to add more functionality to the platform than what is currently available in fiat currencies and stablecoins. Future support should include tokenised deposits and even agentic commerce with a view to the infrastructure for payment systems that joins a variety of money, both regulated and digital, together.

title: Crypto Biz: Wall Street closes at 4. Tokenized stocks keep trading
summary: Tokenized stocks are drawing trading activity beyond Wall Street hours, while Bitcoin miners confront costly AI expansion and new accounting rules could benefit stablecoins.
content:
Tokenization is beginning to reshape traditional financial markets, with stocks increasingly in focus. Much of the attention has centered on the $3.3 billion in tokenized equities now onchain, according to RWA.xyz, but one of the biggest innovations may be what happens before Wall Street opens and after it closes.

According to the latest industry data, more than 70% of tokenized stock trading volume on BNB Chain now occurs outside regular US market hours, with similar patterns emerging on Solana and Base.

Tokenized equities allow investors to trade US stocks across time zones without waiting for Wall Street’s opening bell, potentially changing how liquidity is distributed throughout the day.

However, many platforms driving this activity remain off-limits to American investors, even as US regulators begin to make room for tokenized stock trading.

This week’s Crypto Biz looks at tokenized stock trading, the economics of Bitcoin mining, proposed accounting rules that could make it easier for companies to treat stablecoins as cash equivalents, and Strive’s expanding Bitcoin treasury.

Tokenized stocks find an audience beyond Wall Street’s trading hours

Most tokenized stock trading on Solana and BNB Chain now takes place outside regular US market hours, suggesting that around-the-clock access is becoming a major selling point for equities issued onchain.

According to Blockworks data cited by The Kobeissi Letter, more than 70% of tokenized stock trading volume on BNB Chain occurs outside the traditional 9:30 am to 4:00 pm Eastern trading window. The figure is 63% on Solana and nearly 60% on Base.

Activity is also picking up. Jupiter reported a 50% month-over-month increase in tokenized asset trading volume, while RWA.xyz data showed the value of tokenized stocks climbing 15% over the past 30 days to nearly $3.3 billion.

The trend comes as the US Securities and Exchange Commission’s innovation exemption opens the door for qualifying platforms to trade tokenized US-listed stocks on public blockchains, subject to disclosure and shareholder protection requirements. However, existing offerings such as xStocks and Ondo Global Markets remain largely unavailable to US investors, limiting domestic participation in the growing market.

Source: The Kobeissi Letter

Strive adds 3,311 Bitcoin as investors exercise $208 million in warrants

Bitcoin treasury company Strive increased its holdings by more than 11% last week, using proceeds from warrant exercises to expand its cryptocurrency reserves while increasing Bitcoin exposure per share.

In a Tuesday filing with the SEC, Strive disclosed that it purchased 3,311 BTC during the week ending Oct. 9 at an average price of roughly $84,500 per coin. The purchases brought its total holdings to 32,773 BTC, making it the fifth-largest publicly traded corporate Bitcoin holder.

CEO Matt Cole said investors exercised $208 million in warrants, with about $15.3 million still outstanding ahead of Tuesday’s expiration.

Strive also amended its governing documents to establish a binding $100 minimum issuance price for its SATA preferred shares, which were trading at $99.40. Meanwhile, Bitcoin traded near $83,300, below Strive’s average purchase price for the week, while its common stock, ASST, was little changed at $27.52.

Source: Matt Cole

Bitcoin miners face steep financing costs in AI expansion

Bitcoin mining companies expanding into artificial intelligence and high-performance computing face a widening gap in borrowing costs as lenders examine the risks of large-scale data center projects.

According to BlocksBridge Consulting’s Miner Weekly, securing AI customers is only part of the challenge. Miners also need billions of dollars to build facilities, purchase equipment and secure power infrastructure, with financing terms increasingly dependent on the customer and likelihood of project completion.

The differences are evident in recent deals. IREN secured $3.65 billion in financing in June at a blended interest rate of 6%, followed by another $2.4 billion in August at a fixed 9% rate. The agreements cover different projects, however, making direct comparisons difficult.

The financing needs are substantial. A June BlocksBridge analysis citing VanEck estimated that publicly traded Bitcoin miners required $50 billion to fund their AI infrastructure ambitions. IREN alone faced a $21.1 billion funding gap, followed by Riot Platforms at $7.2 billion and HIVE Digital Technologies at $4.6 billion.

US accounting proposal could give stablecoins a corporate boost

A proposed change to US accounting standards could make stablecoins more attractive to corporate treasuries by allowing qualifying tokens to be treated as cash equivalents on company balance sheets, according to a report from payments blockchain Tempo.

Under current accounting practices, stablecoin holdings may not count toward a company’s reported cash reserves, potentially affecting liquidity ratios and loan covenants even when the tokens are fully backed by US dollars.

The Financial Accounting Standards Board (FASB) proposal could change that, though Tempo noted that companies would need direct redemption rights with stablecoin issuers to qualify. For example, simply purchasing USDC through a cryptocurrency exchange would not necessarily meet that requirement.

Coinbase already classified USDC and other payment stablecoins as cash equivalents in its 2025 annual report, supported by its redemption arrangement with Circle.

The proposal is open for public comment until Nov. 19, after which FASB will review the feedback before determining the final rules and their effective date.

Crypto Biz is your weekly pulse on the business behind blockchain and crypto, delivered directly to your inbox every Thursday.

title: Ripple Brings RLUSD to Cross River Bank as Garlinghouse Backs Evernorth’s XRP Strategy
summary: Ripple is expanding the XRP Ledger’s role in payments as Cross River Bank integrates RLUSD, while CEO Brad Garlinghouse backs Evernorth’s plans for broader XRP investment products.
content:
Skip to content
Assets: XRP

Ripple is expanding the XRP Ledger’s role in payments as Cross River Bank integrates RLUSD, while CEO Brad Garlinghouse backs Evernorth’s plans for broader XRP investment products.

Announced on October 15, the Cross River partnership integrates Ripple USD (RLUSD) into the bank’s proprietary Core Operating System. The arrangement allows fintech clients to access stablecoin payments through a single API alongside traditional payment services, including ACH transfers, wire payments, and real-time payment networks. It is designed to simplify access to blockchain-based settlement without requiring businesses to build their own blockchain infrastructure.

Ripple is integrating RLUSD on the XRP Ledger into Cross River Bank’s payment system, giving fintechs access through a single API. Source: @Ripple via X

The development coincides with Garlinghouse’s remarks at Evernorth’s Nasdaq closing bell ceremony on October 14, where he discussed Ripple’s contribution of XRP and the investment firm’s plans for the broader XRP ecosystem. Together, the developments highlight two approaches to expanding institutional participation: integrating stablecoins into existing banking infrastructure and exploring investment strategies built around XRP. 

RLUSD is backed one-to-one by US dollars and equivalent reserve assets, with issuance handled by a trust company supervised by the New York State Department of Financial Services. Cross River said RLUSD’s market capitalization had exceeded $2.5 billion, with more than $1 billion issued on the XRP Ledger. The network supports transaction settlement in approximately three to five seconds at a fraction of a cent, providing the technical foundation for around-the-clock transfers. 

Ripple Supports Evernorth’s XRP Strategy

Garlinghouse said Ripple’s XRP contribution to Evernorth reflects its broader effort to support the digital asset’s ecosystem and the businesses developing applications around it. He also reiterated that Ripple sees opportunities across multiple blockchain networks, rather than limiting its activities to a single chain.

Brad Garlinghouse discusses Ripple’s XRP contribution to Evernorth to support the community and on-chain activity during the closing bell ceremony. Source: @Vet_X0 via X

“We do believe in a multi-chain world,” Garlinghouse said during the ceremony, according to remarks shared by XRP Ledger validator Vet. He also expressed confidence that the XRP Ledger would develop distinctive uses within the digital asset industry, particularly as payment infrastructure and institutional services expand.

He highlighted Evernorth’s leadership under Asheesh Birla, whom he praised for his experience in strategy, talent development, and business management. Garlinghouse’s comments framed Ripple’s support as an investment in both the people developing the ecosystem and the potential applications they aim to bring to market.

Evernorth completed its business combination with Armada Acquisition Corp. II on October 9, subsequently beginning Nasdaq trading under the ticker XRPN on October 12. At closing, the company reported holdings of approximately 473 million XRP and about $300 million in gross cash proceeds, before transaction expenses. Its investor group includes Ripple, Arrington Capital, SBI Group, Pantera Capital, Kraken, and GSR. 

Evernorth Eyes Yield Opportunities and Institutional Products

Garlinghouse also discussed the potential for Evernorth to develop investment products that go beyond traditional XRP buy-and-hold strategies. Such offerings could combine activity on the XRP Ledger with financial strategies conducted outside the blockchain, giving institutional investors additional ways to participate in the XRP economy.

“You’re going to see some interesting leverage and yield opportunities, some on-chain, some off-chain,” Garlinghouse said. He did not identify specific products or provide a launch timeline during the remarks. The statement therefore outlines a potential direction for Evernorth’s strategy rather than confirming that particular yield products are available. 

Evernorth’s stated business strategy provides further context. The company plans to deploy capital across the XRP ecosystem, support infrastructure development, and pursue institutional and decentralized finance (DeFi) strategies designed to increase the amount of XRP represented by each share over time. Its public listing also creates a stock-market route for investors seeking exposure to an XRP-focused treasury company without directly holding the token. These objectives remain subject to execution, market conditions, and the risks associated with digital assets.

Ripple’s Contribution Aligns With Its Ecosystem Goals

Ripple’s support for Evernorth and its partnership with Cross River address different parts of the XRP ecosystem. The bank integration focuses on using RLUSD for payments and settlement within existing financial infrastructure, while Evernorth intends to deploy capital toward XRP-related applications and investment strategies. Neither announcement establishes that the two initiatives are directly connected, but both reflect efforts to expand the asset ecosystem’s institutional reach.

The Cross River Bank and Ripple partnership combines traditional payment systems with stablecoin functionality, offering businesses more flexible payment solutions. Source: @crossriverbank via X

For Cross River, the practical objective is to make stablecoin transfers accessible through infrastructure that fintech businesses already use. Adam Goller, the bank’s head of fintech banking, said the partnership “eliminates that complexity and makes payments simpler.” The integration supports transfers between US dollars and RLUSD, cross-border payments, and treasury movements around the clock. However, Cross River stated that the service is currently available only in a limited number of US states. 

Ripple’s contribution to Evernorth, meanwhile, supports a model that combines XRP holdings with participation in the wider digital asset economy. Whether this approach generates sustainable returns will depend on the company’s execution and the performance of its investment activities. Similarly, the potential benefits of RLUSD integration will depend on adoption by eligible fintech clients and the payment volumes moving through the platform.

Taken together, the developments highlight Ripple’s efforts to expand the practical uses of its digital asset ecosystem through banking integrations and institutional investment vehicles. The longer-term outcome will depend on whether these initiatives translate into sustained payment activity, broader institutional participation, and viable financial products.

RLUSD payments are becoming part of the banking infrastructure fintechs already use.

  • XRPL Settlement Takes 3 – 5 Seconds

    • Ripple Expands Institutional Stablecoin Access

Cross River Adds RLUSD to Its Core Banking Infrastructure

Cross River will embed RLUSD as another payment channel on their banking platform, inherent with transactions taking place on the XRP ledger. The aim is to enable businesses to settle blockchain without having to construct and maintain their very own blockchain infrastructure.

With one API connection, fintechs can easily pivot between USD and RLUSD, support cross-border transfers and treasury payments, and still utilize traditional rails like ACH, wire transfer and real-time payment services.

Basic integration will decrease the number of businesses needing separate providers when transferring funds across borders, Cross River said.

Read More: Ripple and Privy Bring XRP Wallets to XRPL After $1T Moved Across 8M Accounts

XRPL Settlement Takes 3 – 5 Seconds

The XRP Ledger serves as the settlement layer for the integration. Cross River claims that the transaction can settle in about 3-5 seconds, with a cost of just a few cents and it can run around the clock. To date the network has been processing over $1.3 trillion of settlement value.

This provides greater flexibility for the issuers and acquirers to complete payments throughout the day rather than waiting for standard banking procedures at cut off time.

A model that could also enable funds to pass outside of the normal business hours for the treasury team without interrupting bank payment services.

RLUSD Market Cap Surpasses $2.5 Billion

The collaboration is coming at a time when Ripple’s stablecoin is rapidly expanding. The market capitalization of the company, RLUSD, stands at more than $2.5 billion, with more than $1 billion directly on the XRP Ledger, Cross River said.

Instead of creating its own ecosystem, Ripple wants to integrate the stablecoin with infrastructure used by banks and fintech companies. That strategy is reflected in the Cross River setup: RLUSD sits alongside conventional dollar payment rails instead of replacing them entirely.

Read More: Ripple Lands 4th Korea Deal, Bringing Custody and Tokenization to Meritz Securities

Ripple Expands Institutional Stablecoin Access

Ripple has been gradually shifting its focus to the financial institutions, which are regulated.

It now has more than 85 licenses worldwide to supply products that include payments, custody, treasury management and other institutional services.

The integration opens up yet another regulated distribution channel for RLUSD and provides fintech clients with a straight path to the XRPL settlement directly through the banking ecosystem.

The service is only offered in some U.S. states and will expand to more States over time as Cross River expands access.

title: Big Tech's AI auditors will only see what they're shown
summary: If the White House accord's audits are going to be worth anything, auditors should be able to choose what they test, writes Samuel Vance-Law, head of research at the Decentralization Research Center.
content:
Oct 16, 2026, 10:58 a.m. EDT

4 min read

Last week, six of the most powerful AI companies in the world promised the White House they would let outsiders check their work.

On Sept. 29, Nvidia, OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, Meta and xAI signed an accord on the most advanced AI models that U.S. President Donald Trump called "morally binding." Each company has promised it will "partner with an independent external auditor or evaluator" and have independent board members review the auditors' reports and make sure problems get fixed.

Outside audits are a good idea, and I'm glad to see them in there. But the accord says nothing about who chooses the auditors, what they can examine or whether any findings are made public; there's no penalty for ignoring it. As it stands, each company picks its own auditor and decides what that auditor gets to look at.

In 2000, Enron paid accounting firm Arthur Andersen — once part of the so-called “Big Five” of international accounting firms, now the “Big Four” after Arthur Andersen’s implosion — $25 million to audit its books and another $27 million for tax and consulting work. Within two years, both firms had collapsed. Congress responded with the Sarbanes-Oxley Act, which took the choice of auditor away from management, stopped auditors from selling most other services to the companies they audit and set up a public board to inspect the auditors themselves.

Andersen failed not due to a deficit in expertise, but in an incentive to look hard at a client paying it $52 million in a single year. Voluntary pledges in the AI industry don't have a great record, either. In 2023, the leading AI companies made a set of voluntary commitments to the White House, including letting outside experts test their systems before release. When researchers at Stanford, Harvard and Brown went back and scored 16 companies against those commitments, the average came to 53%. On the promise to help outsiders find and report problems, eight of the 16 scored zero.

Even when outside testing does happen, the developer sets the terms. METR, a nonprofit that tests AI models, wrote that its testing of OpenAI's o3 model before release was "conducted over only three weeks," with "limited access to information about the model" and no view of the model's step-by-step reasoning.

To be fair to OpenAI, it allowed the testing in the first place. But it shows how much rides on what a company chooses to share.

A trained AI model is essentially a very large file of numbers, often costing more than $100 million to produce, and whoever has a copy has the model. Handing copies to outsiders is a security risk. Until recently, that left testers with an awkward choice, which Google DeepMind has described well: either the testers hand over their questions, so the company sees the exam in advance, or the company hands over its model.

In August, DeepMind showed a way around that. Working with Singapore's AI Safety Institute and three other outside groups, it ran what it called the world's first double-blind test of an AI model, on the same principle as a double-blind drug trial. The test ran on sealed computer hardware, so the outside testers never saw the model and Google never saw their questions. Google says each side can check mathematically that its material stayed private.

It also moves the trust onto the hardware. Last year, researchers broke into this kind of sealed hardware with less than $1,000 of equipment, although they needed physical access to the server to do it. That's worth taking seriously. But it's a much smaller problem than "we can't let anyone near the model," and it can be managed by being careful about who controls the machines.

For our report, "Alternatives to Concentrated AI," published this week by the Decentralization Research Center, my co-author Kyle Bligen and I interviewed 36 people and mapped nearly 30 working alternatives to concentrated control over AI. Our main finding was this one: outsiders can now scrutinize advanced AI without taking possession of the model or its data.

If the accord's audits are going to be worth anything, auditors should choose what they test, now that they can do so without taking a copy of the model. Companies should also say who their auditors are and what the audits covered, even if the detailed findings stay private. Public companies have named their auditors for decades without giving away trade secrets. And the board committees reading these reports should answer to someone outside the company. Sarbanes-Oxley created an inspector for the inspectors. The accord has nothing like it, and Congress should decide what fills that gap.

Note: The views expressed in this column are those of the author and do not necessarily reflect those of CoinDesk, Inc. or its owners and affiliates.

title: Kalshi Turns Local Ballot Data into a Market Discovery Tool
summary:
Kalshi has added My Ballot to its 2026 Midterms Hub, using Ballotpedia’s election data to show visitors the races on their own ballots. Where Kalshi has an active contract, the guide displays its market price alongside the contest. 
Kalshi says more than 80% of Midterms Hub visitors do not trade, th...
content:
2026-10-16T16:06:00.000+02:00

Friday, 16/10/2026 | 14:06 GMT by Tanya Chepkova

  • Kalshi says more than 80% of its Midterms Hub visitors do not trade, making election information valuable to the platform in its own right.
  • Politics generated $169 million in July trading volume versus $31.4 billion for sports. Kalshi has not shown whether personalised ballot lookups lead to trades.

Kalshi has added My Ballot to its 2026 Midterms Hub, using Ballotpedia’s election data to show visitors the races on their own ballots. Where Kalshi has an active contract, the guide displays its market price alongside the contest.

Kalshi says more than 80% of Midterms Hub visitors do not trade, they come for data. People checking local election information can therefore encounter political markets without searching for a contract.

My Ballot makes the guide more useful to that audience while putting relevant markets in view. It is available on Kalshi’s website and mobile app and will cover every race with an active Kalshi market through Election Day.

From Address to Election Market

My Ballot visitor enters the address, and the system identifies the races and ballot measures relevant to that location, using Ballotpedia’s Sample Ballot Lookup data. Kalshi then checks those contests against its active election markets and displays a market price wherever it finds a match.

Thus, Ballotpedia tells visitors what they can vote on, while Kalshi shows how traders are pricing the outcome. Kalshi’s VoteHub already brings market prices together with polling, campaign-finance data and past results.

My Ballot reorganises that material around the visitor’s own ballot. Instead of starting with a national race and searching for a local connection, visitors can begin with the contests relevant to them and follow through to a market where one exists.

Politics in a Sports-Led Market

This personalised approach arrives at a different moment for Kalshi’s political markets.

In 2024, politics was the platform’s largest trading category around that year’s presidential election, but it had to fight for it with the Commodity Futures Trading Commission in court.

Now its business looks different. Since then, sports has moved far ahead, while political trading on Kalshi remained below $300 million a month throughout the period ending in July 2026 covered by Pew Research Center. In July alone, politics generated $169 million in volume against $31.4 billion for sports.

Kalshi presents My Ballot as a way to help visitors understand local elections. In a platform now dominated by sports trading, the guide could also make political markets easier to find.

Will Information Lead to Trades?

Organising market discovery around something the visitor came to do might be an efficient customer acquisition strategy. My Ballot starts with a practical question about a person’s ballot and introduces a related contract only when one exists.

What happens after that introduction is still unknown. Kalshi has not released data showing how often visitors who find a local race go on to trade its contract.

For now, My Ballot establishes an information-led route to political markets, not a proven way to acquire traders.

content:
Could anyone actually break Bitcoin? Micah Warren, associate professor of mathematics at the University of Oregon and author of Bitcoin: A Game-Theoretic Analysis, joins Grace Remington and Sean Hagan to break down Bitcoin’s security through the lens of game theory. He explains why miner incentives are one of the main things holding Bitcoin up, and why classic reorg and double-spend attacks are unlikely today.

title: FCA Flags High Overnight Fees as Only 12% of CFD Firms Change Charges
summary:
The UK Financial
Conduct Authority has warned that some CFD brokers may be charging retail
clients excessive overnight funding fees and failing to explain these costs
clearly. The regulator also questioned charges on matched or hedged positions,
where clients hold open buy and sell CFDs on the same ...
content:
2026-10-16T14:14:18.174+02:00

Friday, 16/10/2026 | 12:14 GMT by Tareq Sikder

  • The regulator surveyed 81 CFD firms and found limited pricing changes, opaque funding mark-ups and inadequate client disclosures.
  • CFD firms are expected to make fee information more prominent and clearer across websites, apps and deal entry screens.

The UK Financial Conduct Authority has warned that some CFD brokers may be charging retail clients excessive overnight funding fees and failing to explain these costs clearly. The regulator also questioned charges on matched or hedged positions, where clients hold open buy and sell CFDs on the same asset.

London's trading industry is coming home!

The findings follow the FCA's November 2025 review, which identified inconsistent charges and weaknesses in how CFD providers assessed fair value under the Consumer Duty. Finance Magnates previously examined the regulator's concerns about consumer protection and the pressure on brokers to justify their pricing.

The FCA surveyed 81 firms in May 2026 to assess their response to the review. Most had made changes or planned to do so, but only 12% said they had changed their charges.

Most CFD Brokers Keep Funding Fees Unchanged

Most firms focused on explaining existing rates rather than changing them. Measures taken or planned by the 12% included reducing fees on matched positions, lowering charges for certain asset groups and introducing interest payments on cash balances.

The FCA said some funding fees appeared high relative to prevailing base rates and peer comparisons. Mark-ups remained largely opaque, while only a minority of firms had added annual percentage rates to help clients compare financing costs.

FCA Demands Clearer CFD Funding Fee Disclosures

Most firms continued to apply overnight fees to matched positions, often using the same funding charge spread as for ordinary long or short trades. The FCA questioned whether this offered fair value, particularly when firms encouraged matched positions through reduced or waived margin requirements . Clients may incur additional spreads and funding fees by keeping both trades open.

The regulator also called for clearer fee disclosures on websites and deal entry screens, including explanations of how charges are calculated. It will continue monitoring firms' pricing practices and contact individual providers where necessary.

title: BC.GAME’s BC Engine surpasses $10 million in rewards in six months after launch
summary: PRNewswire, PRNewswire, 16th October 2026, Chainwire
content:
Skip to content

PRNewswire, PRNewswire, 16th October 2026, Chainwire

Launched in April 2026, BC Engine has reached a major milestone in cumulative rewards, strengthening its role as a core value-sharing mechanism within the BC.GAME ecosystem

BELIZE CITY, Belize, Oct. 16, 2026 /PRNewswire/ — BC.GAME – the award-winning global online entertainment platform – can announce that its BC Engine has surpassed 10 million BCD in cumulative rewards, equivalent to more than US$10 million, just six months after its launch on April 8, 2026.

The milestone highlights the rapid growth of BC Engine, which has evolved from an hourly reward mechanism into an increasingly important pillar of the BC.GAME ecosystem, connecting $BC holders, platform activity, and gaming partners through recurring value distribution.

From launch to $10 million in six months

Since its introduction, BC Engine has recorded consistent growth in cumulative rewards.

On May 28, participating $BC holders had earned more than 2.1 million BCD. By July 28, cumulative rewards had exceeded 5 million BCD, reaching 8.6 million BCD by September 18.

Now, just six months after launch, the figure has surpassed 10 million BCD, representing nearly fivefold growth since late May.

BC Engine allows eligible $BC holders to earn BCD rewards through hourly settlement rounds. The reported US$10 million represents rewards already earned through completed settlements, rather than projected returns or changes in $BC’s market price.

Building a stronger BC.GAME ecosystem

Beyond the milestone itself, BC Engine is becoming a key component of BC.GAME’s long-term ecosystem strategy.

Unlike conventional promotional rewards, BC Engine connects platform activity with recurring value distribution, creating ongoing incentives for participation and strengthening the utility of $BC.

Through the introduction of Engine Nodes, partners including BC Originals, Croco Gaming and BETBY, have become part of the expanding reward ecosystem, connecting different gaming products and providers through a shared value distribution mechanism.

For users, BC Engine provides recurring rewards and transparent settlement records. For ecosystem partners, it creates deeper connections with the platform and its community. Together, these mechanisms are designed to strengthen long-term engagement, build trust and support a more interconnected gaming ecosystem.

Supporting BC.GAME’s global expansion

BC Engine’s growth comes alongside BC.GAME’s continued international expansion.

In 2026, BC.GAME strengthened its regulated presence in Mexico and partnered with Mexican football legend Guillermo “Memo” Ochoa as a brand ambassador, reinforcing its localization strategy in Latin America.

As BC.GAME continues to develop its international operations, BC Engine serves as an increasingly important mechanism connecting platform growth, $BC utility and ecosystem participation.

Surpassing US$10 million in just six months marks a significant step toward BC.GAME’s vision of building a more connected, participation-driven gaming ecosystem.

Adrian Chen, Senior Legal Counsel at BC.GAME, said: “Achieving 10 million BCD in rewards in the first six months of the BC Engine demonstrates the success and rapid growth of our rewards programme and adoption amongst players. We look forward to rewarding even more BCD in the coming months as we continue to scale our ecosystem globally.”

About BC.GAME

BC.GAME is a global online gaming and entertainment platform offering casino, sportsbook and digital asset-based products across international markets where permitted.

Since 2017, BC.GAME has developed a crypto-native entertainment ecosystem focused on product innovation, community participation and global partnerships. Its native token, $BC, powers ecosystem utilities including BC Engine, which provides recurring BCD rewards to eligible participants.

For more information, visit https://bc.game/bc.

title: UPTECH Highlights Unified Brokerage Infrastructure Following UF Awards Nomination
summary: UPTECH, a fintech firm providing institutional technology infrastructure for FX, CFD, and multi-asset brokerages, is marking its UF AWARDS APAC 2026 nomination by highlighting the integrated architecture behind its technology offering. The company views the nomination as industry recognition of its ...
content:
2026-10-16T12:33:25.179+02:00

Friday, 16/10/2026 | 10:33 GMT by UPTECH

Disclaimer

  • The fintech firm brings trading, risk management, client support, and Web3 payments together to support institutional growth across global markets.

UPTECH, a fintech firm providing institutional technology infrastructure for FX, CFD, and multi-asset brokerages, is marking its UF AWARDS APAC 2026 nomination by highlighting the integrated architecture behind its technology offering. The company views the nomination as industry recognition of its technical approach to helping financial institutions modernize operations and support growth.

For brokerage leaders, expansion requires more than additional trading capacity. Execution, risk oversight, client service, and payments must work together as operations become more complex. UPTECH addresses these requirements through a unified, modular ecosystem designed to reduce operational friction while giving institutions flexibility in how they develop their brokerage infrastructure.

Connecting core brokerage operations

The UPTECH ecosystem brings together five core products. CTOTrader provides a multi-asset trading platform solution, while UPBASE serves as an all-in-one web trading client platform. Together, they connect the trading environment with the client-facing experience within the broader infrastructure.

UPSHIELD adds enterprise risk management and on-chain anti-money laundering intelligence, placing risk oversight alongside the ecosystem’s trading and payment capabilities. UPTOPAY supports Web3 payments through a decentralized, multi-asset smart contract payment protocol. UPAGENT completes the offering with an intelligent helpdesk and ticket system for brokerage customer support.

By bringing these functions into an integrated architecture, UPTECH aims to reduce the complexity of coordinating disconnected systems. Its modular approach allows brokerages to align technology adoption with their operational priorities, with enterprise security and continuity central to the company’s infrastructure philosophy.

Supporting clients across the markets

For institutions serving Asia-Pacific, the Middle East, and Africa, a consistent client experience must also accommodate different languages and local market needs. UPTECH’s approach to AI-powered localization addresses this challenge through tools designed to help support teams respond in the languages their clients use.

Within UPAGENT, a Bring Your Own Key framework enables brokerages to connect their preferred large language models. Combined with custom knowledge bases, the system supports real-time, bidirectional translation tailored to local dialects, generates context-aware replies, and executes workflow actions in native languages. These capabilities help brokerages extend multilingual service without increasing local support staffing proportionally.

UPTECH’s focus is on applying fintech innovation to practical institutional requirements: coordinated operations, enterprise risk oversight, and responsive client service. The UF Awards nomination marks a milestone in that work as the company continues to position unified infrastructure as a foundation for brokerage growth.
